7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

The Credit Limit Breach Rule

  • When an order is placed on credit, the system always checks:

$$\text{Net Amount Owed} + \text{New Order Total} \le \text{Customer Credit Limit}$$

  • Net amount owed means open invoices less credits not yet used. It is not the customer card's display balance. The company's Customer credit display only decides whether people see the limit alone (_Static_) or the limit less what is owed (_Running_); it never changes this check.
  • If the calculation exceeds the limit:
  • When the company allows proceeding beyond available credit, an approval workflow decides if one is configured; with no workflow, the order is created.
  • Otherwise, when an Approval Workflow for a credit override is configured and the kind of sale asks for approval, the order waits with its stock reserved until an approver releases it.
  • Otherwise order creation is blocked with a message naming the credit limit; nothing is saved or charged.

Quotes requested on the web shop

A package set to Request a quote (or Either) in Pricing → Packages lets a shopper ask for a quote from the product page. It arrives as a draft quote with Requested on the web shop in place of _Created by_ (list and detail), the shopper's name, email and phone, the date they need it and their message in the internal notes. The price is worked out from the package, never typed by the shopper. Staff review, send and convert it like any other quote. The company's own email address is alerted when a request arrives (and the shopper gets a confirmation if they gave an email address), so keep that address set in Company Setup. See the packages section of guide 05 for the setting.

Sales Orders (/admin/sales-orders)

Where staff take an order for a customer: by phone, at the counter for later, or for an account. Behind two permissions: _Sales orders: read_ (the list) and _Sales orders: create_ (taking one).

  • The list: the sales orders staff took, newest first, 25 at a time with Show more; Find a sales order searches the order number or the customer's name. Each row shows the number, customer, date, total, status, payment status and Waiting for approval when it is held. Open order opens that sales order over this list; closing it returns here.
  • New sales order: choose the customer (search by name, number, email or phone). The card under it shows where they stand: a credit account with its days, the credit limit, amount owed and, when the running display is on, available credit, plus blocked and overdue warnings; a cash customer says so. With the static display, only the limit is shown. Add products (search; the list price shows) and packages (the same builder the shop uses, every option choosable; a package is sold in whole servings). Choose the expected payment (a label: M-Pesa, Pesapal, Jenga, KCB Buni; the money is received by receipt) and, if needed, the day it is needed on. Where the company's setting allows it, Hold the stock until this order is paid appears. Place order.
  • The lines (the same on Sales Orders, Credit Sales and Sales Invoices): the product search sits above the lines, and each line is laid out like an invoice with four named parts: Item (with its list price), Quantity, Unit price and Line total. On a phone every line is a card with the same four names. Under the lines the total is shown as Before tax, Tax and Total, worked out by the server for this customer as you type (until a customer is chosen, only the total at list prices is shown, and the screen says why). A quantity of nothing or a price of nothing is refused in words beside the box.
  • Change the price of an item (permission Sales orders / Credit sales / Sales invoices: change the price of an item, given on purpose to the people who need it): the Unit price is a box. Type the new price and press Enter or leave the box; the line total follows. The line says price changed, and the round arrow brings the list price back. The server holds the new price to the price floors and to the person's own limit below list price, and refuses it in words otherwise. A person without the permission sees the price but cannot change it, and a price sent anyway is ignored.
  • Give a discount on an item (two things must both be true: the company has allowed it for the branch under Selling Documents > Discount typed by staff for that document, and the person has the permission offer a discount on an item for that document): the Discount column has a button for a percentage or an amount off each unit. The charged price shows with the price it came from struck through. A person who may not see no discount control at all, and a discount sent anyway is refused in words. A discount is never offered on a package line, and it is held to the price floors and the person's override limit like a changed price. On a line with a discount the price box is read-only; remove the discount to type a price.
  • What happens when you place it: the server prices the order for that customer (the browser never sends a price) and applies the company's Selling Documents settings for sales orders: the credit check and limit, what happens over it, the credit days on the invoice's due date, approval, discounts, when the stock leaves and whether the tax invoice is made with the order. The limit check always uses net amount owed, even when the screen shows only the limit. The company's proceeding beyond available credit setting can also let an over-limit order reach an approval workflow or be created when no workflow exists. A refusal is shown in words ("… would exceed the credit limit of …") and nothing is placed. When an approval is needed the order is placed waiting for approval and says so.
  • On account is not a choice here: a customer's credit comes from their account (limit and days), whatever the expected payment. Selling to an account customer by "on account" belongs to the Credit Sales module.
  • Related documents: an order's details (in Web Shop Orders) show Related documents: the quote it was made from, and the invoices raised for it, with numbers, totals and dates. A quote that has become an order shows Became the order with its number. Deliveries and credit notes have their own panels on the order.

Selling with no connection (Cash Sales, when switched on in Settings, Offline selling)

Available only when the company has switched it on, for cash sales by a person with an open shift opened while online.

  • Getting ready: while online with a shift open, the Cash Sales screen keeps the till ready on its own (it says Ready to sell with no connection, refreshed every few minutes): it keeps the offline till page and its files in the browser (a service worker), the list prices of what may be sold at the counter, the ways of paying for this branch, and the shift's signing key. A browser that cannot keep these (private windows, blocked storage) says so and cannot sell offline.
  • The offline till (/admin/cash-sales/offline, linked from Cash Sales): shows Connected or No connection: selling from what the till kept, how many sales are waiting to be sent, and sells like the counter: add products (found on the till itself), quantities, cash with change, M-Pesa or card (with its reference), a mix of up to four. It never prices by rule: the customer is charged the kept list price; discounts, price lists, packages and named customers need the connection.
  • Complete sale keeps the sale on the till, signed with the shift's key so a change afterwards is seen, and shows a slip with the till's own reference (OFF-<till>-0007) and "tax receipt to follow". The slip is not the tax receipt: keep it until the receipt is printed. If the shift's offline limit is used up the till refuses another offline sale and says why.
  • When the connection returns the till sends its sales one at a time, in the order they were rung up, on its own, and shows each one's real receipt number. Sending a sale twice never makes two. The sale is accepted at the price the customer was charged; if it differs from today's price, or a product is no longer sold at the counter, the sale is accepted and flagged (Needs a look).
  • What cannot be made is kept, never lost: a sale past the limits, changed after it was signed, or into a shift that is already closed is refused with the reason; a sale whose stock is not there (or whose way of paying is gone) is parked (Not made yet). Both are listed under Offline sales to look at on Cash Sales (for people who may read cash sales). A supervisor can Look at a flagged sale, Try again a parked one once the stock is put right, or Give up a parked or refused sale with a reason that is kept. A shift cannot be closed while a sale of it is parked, nor while sales are still waiting on the till (the Shifts screen says how many).
  • A lost device: a sale that never left a device that is never reconnected is not in the books, so the till will count over at the close: a supervisor looks into it (the decision log shows every offline sale that did arrive).
  • Not in this release: returns, opening or closing a shift, credit customers, price rules, and packages offline; a second till taking over another's waiting sales.

Invoicing in parts (Sales invoices, when switched on in Settings, Partial billing)

Available only when the company has switched it on (its own permission and screen in Settings), for sales orders that have no tax invoice yet, are approved and are not cancelled, and whose delivery (if any) is billed with the goods.

  • Raise an invoice: choose the order; the Invoicing in parts card shows each line with ordered, invoiced and left, and the part invoices already made (number, total, whether it finishes the order, signing status, PDF).
  • Invoice these quantities: type how many of each line to invoice (decimals only where the product allows them; never more than is left). The card shows the invoice's total as the server works it out and refuses a quantity that is too big in words, before anything is raised. Each part is a full tax invoice: numbered in order for the order and from the same gap-free tax invoice series as every other invoice, signed with KRA on its own, at the order's own prices.
  • Invoice what is left: takes every line's remainder and finishes the order: this invoice also carries the delivery charge and any rounding, so the invoices of an order always add up to the order to the cent. Once an order is finished it is no longer offered.
  • Never both: an order with a whole-order tax invoice cannot take a part invoice, and an order with part invoices refuses the whole-order invoice ("invoiced in parts: invoice what is left"). Two people pressing at once cannot invoice the same units twice.
  • Corrections: an invoice is never edited; a credit note is raised against one part invoice (the order's credit panel asks Credit which invoice) and can only credit that part's lines at its amounts, with returned goods, restock and refund following the usual credit note flow. A delivery charge carried by the finishing part is not credited line by line.
  • Part invoices in the list: Sales invoices shows them as Part invoice (filter Part invoices) with their own signing and credited status. Emailing a part invoice again is not offered yet (download the PDF).

Where a product or package is offered (Offered in, on the product)

Every product and package carries an Offered in list on its edit window (Media tab): Sales quotes, Sales orders, Credit sales, Cash sales (the counter) and Sales invoices, all ticked unless you change them. A product that is not ticked for a document is not found by that document's product search, not shown in the quote editor's catalogue, and refused in words ("X is not offered in cash sales. Change where it is offered on the product") if it is sent anyway, on every staff document and on quote lines and quote templates. An order made from a quote is not asked again, because the quote already checked it. A package is a product, so the same list controls where it can be sold. The web shop keeps its own switch, Show in the web shop. Use it for items you only sell to account customers (untick Cash sales), only at the counter (untick the others), or only by quote.

Cash Sales (/admin/cash-sales)

The counter: a fast sale paid at once, rung up inside the person's own open shift (see Shifts). Behind two permissions: Cash sales: create (ring up a sale; you only ever sell into your own shift) and Cash sales: read (see every counter sale; without it you see only your own shift's).

  • Before selling: you need an open shift on a till (the screen says so and links to Shifts). A shift whose close is waiting for approval takes no sales; withdraw the close to sell again. The bar at the top shows the till, how many sales so far and what the till should hold.
  • The till screen: the counter is laid out like a point of sale. On the left, one bar that searches by name, SKU or stock code and takes a scanned code (press Enter and an exact code goes straight into the sale; F2 jumps to the bar), category buttons under it, a Your usual row (what this person has sold most in the last 30 days) and picture tiles (a coloured tile with initials when a product has no picture) showing the price, a Low or Out mark for stock and a count badge of how many are already in the sale; out-of-stock tiles and products with no price cannot be tapped. Services are never "out". Only products offered in Cash Sales and sold on their own appear; a package tile opens its builder (the same as Sales Orders). Tap a tile to add one, tap again for one more. On the right is the sale: each line with its picture-less name, minus and plus buttons, a typed quantity, its price and a remove button, the total the server worked out and a large Pay button (F4). On a phone the sale is behind a bar at the bottom ("View sale · 3 items · KES …") that opens it as a sheet. Customer is optional (empty means the walk-in customer; choose one to have the sale in their name).
  • Change an item's price (permission Cash sales: change an item's price, given on purpose to the people who need it, such as a senior cashier): on each line of the sale the price of one shows with a pencil. Press it, type the new price of one (tax included, as the shelf shows it) and press the tick; the line then says price changed and the total follows. The round arrow puts the list price back. A price can be raised freely. It cannot go below the item's price floor (a floor price on the price list, or a floor rule such as never below cost), and it cannot go further below the list price than the person's own limit (Price floors and override limits, set per role): the sale then says why and the price must be corrected, because a till cannot wait for a supervisor. No promotion is added on top of a price that was typed. The server checks the permission again on every sale, so a price sent by anyone without it is ignored and the list price is charged; the line's price explanation records Price changed at the counter with the old and new price. Someone without the permission sees the price but cannot press it.
  • Give a discount on an item (two things must both be true: the company has allowed it for the branch, and the person has the permission Cash sales: offer a discount on an item, which is not given to anyone by default): the company chooses where, in Settings → Selling Documents → Cash sales → Discount typed by staff (Not offered, At every branch, or Only at the branches chosen, with the branches listed). Where both are true, each line shows a Discount button under its quantity. Press it, choose % (a percentage above 0 and under 100) or KES (an amount off each unit, tax included, as the shelf shows it), type the number and press the tick; the line then says 10% off (or the amount) and the total follows. The cross removes it. A percentage or amount that is not a real discount is refused in words on the line. The discount comes off the price in force (the typed price, if the person also changed it, otherwise the list price) and is held to the same limits as a price change: never below the item's price floor, never further below the list price than the person's own limit (Price floors and override limits, set per role) and never as much as the price itself; the sale then says why and the discount must be reduced, because a till cannot wait for a supervisor. A person without the permission, or a branch the company has not chosen, never sees the button, and the server refuses a discount from anyone else, in words, rather than charging a price nobody expected. A branch left blank on the person's profile counts as the company's default branch. A discount is not offered on a package line, is not available on the offline till, and is never added on top of a promotion (a line with a discount is priced by the discount alone). The order's price explanation records Discount of … given at the counter with the old and new price, and the total of such discounts is kept with the order's discount summary. What the receipt says about it is the company's choice in Settings → Sales → Cash Sales → Discounts on the receipt: only the price charged (the default), one total discount near the end, or the discount under each item (see guide 13). The company's Discounts setting of No discounts switches this off as well. The same setting is meant to reach the other selling points (sales orders, invoices, credit sales) later; until then they offer Not offered only.
  • Hold and bring back: Hold (F8) sets the sale aside while you serve someone else (a name like Sale 1 is made for it; up to ten at a time); On hold (F6) lists them with the first items, Bring back (only when the sale in front of you is empty) or Give up. A held sale is only a list of items and counts: nothing is priced, stock is not touched and nothing is paid until it is brought back and completed, and it is priced afresh when it comes back. It stays with the person and the shift; anything still on hold when the shift closes is given up.
  • Total: worked out by the server with the same pricing as every other sale (price list, discounts, tax) as lines change; the screen never prices anything itself. Until the server has answered, Pay stays off, so a payment is never started on an old total.
  • Payment screen (Pay): the total in large figures and a line saying what is still to pay, paid in full or the change to give. The ways of paying set up for this branch (cash, M-Pesa or card) are big buttons. For cash there are quick buttons: the exact amount and the next amounts a customer is likely to hand over (to the next 50, 100, 500, 1,000 and so on); one tap records it. For M-Pesa or card one tap pays the full amount still owed with that method, and the M-Pesa code or card slip number is asked for where the method needs it (Complete stays off until it is filled). The number pad (or the keyboard) takes any other amount; Add records it. Pay in one way or a mix (up to four): for example 100 in cash and the rest by M-Pesa; remove a payment with its bin button. Only cash can be handed over in excess (change); M-Pesa and card pay exactly. A short payment says by how much and Complete sale stays off.
  • Complete sale: in one step the sale is placed, stock leaves the branch, how it was paid is recorded and the sale is marked paid, the sale is queued to the books (each way of paying lands in its own cash or bank account), and the receipt is the signed tax invoice on the POS receipt series. The screen then shows the change to give in large figures, Print receipt, and New sale.
  • Safe to repeat: each sale has a key made when the screen starts it, so pressing Complete twice, or again after a dropped connection, never counts a sale twice. If a sale was rung up but its payment could not be recorded, the screen says so and the button changes to Finish payment; the shift cannot be closed until it is finished.
  • Full-screen till or inside the admin page: set in Settings & Configuration → Sales → Cash Sales (see 7c). Full-screen gives the whole screen to selling (the admin menu is out of the way) with a slim top bar: the till and shift, Sales (the shift's sales, returns and offline review), Shift and reports and Exit.
  • Sales so far: the shift's (or, with Cash sales: read, all) counter sales, newest first, 25 at a time; Receipt shows or reprints one.
  • Return goods (permission Cash sales: return, normally for a supervisor): the Return button on a paid sale opens the return: enter how many of each line come back (never more than is still returnable; a return can be partial and repeated), Why (a reason from the company's list) and what the customer said, and tick The goods are fit to sell again to put them back in stock (leave it off for damaged goods: the stock stays out and the loss is the business's). Choose how the customer is paid back: cash (handed over from your open shift; asks who takes it, the customer's name when empty) or M-Pesa to a number. Return and refund then, in order: issues a credit note that corrects the tax invoice (signed like any credit note, so the books and the customer account follow), counts the goods back into stock, asks for the refund through the normal refund flow (its approval workflow, limits and posting all apply), and, when the refund is approved at once and is cash, hands the cash back from the open shift (the shift's expected cash goes down by it, shown on the X and Z reports as Cash handed back for returns). A refund that needs approval is left waiting: the return shows under Returns to finish, and once approved, Finish hands the cash over (the person who approved cannot be the one who records the payout). Pressing the button twice, or again after a dropped connection, never credits, restocks or pays twice: a return that stopped part way is finished from where it was. The walk-in customer's refunds are not held by the per-customer limits or the same-amount check (they are many buyers), but the limits per cashier and per phone number still apply. A void is a return of everything on the sale.

Shifts (/admin/shifts)

A shift is one person's time on one till. Cash sales (the Cash Sales module) can only be rung up inside an open shift. Behind four permissions: _Shifts: read_ (see everyone's shifts and reports), _open_ (open a shift and put cash in or take it out), _close_ (close your own) and _supervise_ (close another person's, and close a shift that is out by more than the company allows). Someone without _read_ sees only their own shifts.

  • Open a shift: choose a till (only tills with no shift open, in your branch if you have one) and count the float in the drawer: a box for each note and coin (1,000, 500, 200, 100, 50, 20, 10, 5, 1) with the total growing as you count, or tick _I only have a total_. Open shift. You can have one shift open at a time, and a till one shift at a time.
  • During the shift: the X report shows the opening float, cash sales, cash put in, cash taken out and what the till should hold, any time, without closing anything. Cash in or out records cash put in (for example change from the bank) or taken out (for example buying supplies) with the reason; you cannot take out more than the till holds. Download PDF saves the report (X while open, Z once closed) as a clean A4 document with the shop's name, the till, who opened and closed it and when, the cash worked out line by line, what was taken by M-Pesa and card, the drawer count, the cash put in and taken out, and lines for the cashier and supervisor to sign; Print prints that same document, never the screen around it. Only people who may see that shift's report can make the PDF.
  • Close the shift: count the cash in the drawer. The system works out the difference from what the till should hold. Any difference needs a reason in words. A difference beyond the limit set in Registers is either closed by a supervisor on the spot or sent to approval, as the company chose in Registers; a supervisor may always close another person's shift on the spot. When it goes to approval the shift shows Waiting for approval with the count and reason, no cash can move on it, and the cashier can Withdraw the request and recount; once approved it closes with its Z number, and if it is rejected the shift is open again for a recount. Closing gives the shift its Z report number from the gap-free series and keeps its figures, so the Z report never changes: a closed shift cannot be edited and cash cannot be added to it (the database refuses).
  • Shifts so far: newest first, 25 at a time; each row shows the Z number (or Open), the till, who and when, and Till right or the difference. Open shows its report; Print prints it. A supervisor opening another person's open shift can close it from there.
  • Cash sales taken in the shift are its Cash sales line (net of change), and the X and Z reports show what counter sales took by M-Pesa and card as well, for reconciling against the provider and bank statements. The cash difference is written to the books at the close (see Settings, Registers: the till's cash account and the account for till differences); until those are chosen it waits, and the Z report says so.

Credit Sales (/admin/credit-sales)

Where staff sell to a customer's account: a sale charged to the customer's credit, invoiced at once. Behind two permissions: _Credit sales: read_ (the list) and _Credit sales: create_ (making one).

  • The list: the credit sales, newest first, 25 at a time with Show more; Find a credit sale searches the order number or the customer. It lists the sales staff made on account; a shopper's web shop purchase on account stays in Web Shop Orders even though it is invoiced as a credit sale. Each row shows number, customer, date, total, status, payment status and Waiting for approval when held.
  • New credit sale: only customers with a credit account are offered. The card shows their credit limit, amount owed and, when the running display is on, available credit, their days, and blocked and overdue warnings. Add products and packages (the shop's builder), the day it is needed and, where the company allows it, Hold the stock until this sale is paid. There is no payment to choose: it is on the customer's account terms. Place credit sale.
  • What happens: the server prices it for that customer and applies the company's Selling Documents settings for _Credit sales_: the credit limit is checked against the net amount owed (over it, the company's approval workflows or the over-credit setting decide, or it is refused in words), the invoice falls due on the customer's days, the tax invoice is made with the sale (and automatically once approved if an approval held it, unless _Invoice after approval_ is off), and the stock leaves as that setting says (by default at delivery or collection). A customer without a credit account is refused ("is a cash customer and must pay at the invoice"): use a sales invoice or a sales order for them.
  • Credit hold with release: a sale over the limit is held for approval by a workflow whose condition is the customer being over their credit limit (set up in Approvals); the approver releases it and the invoice follows. With no workflow to ask, it is refused unless the company has switched on proceeding beyond available credit, in which case the order is created.

Sales Invoices (/admin/sales-invoices)

Where staff find, check and raise invoices. Behind three permissions: _Sales invoices: read_ (the list and an invoice's detail), _create_ (raise an invoice) and _send_ (send it again, print or download it).

  • The list: every invoice document, from whatever kind of sale raised it — a sales order that has been invoiced, a credit sale, a web shop order, or a direct sales invoice — newest first, 25 at a time with Show more. Find an invoice searches the invoice number, the order number or the customer; the Kind choice narrows to _Tax invoices_, _Proforma_ or _Delivery_ invoices. Each row shows the number, kind, order, customer, date, total and three things: how KRA signing stands (_Signed with KRA_, _Being signed_, _Waiting to be signed_, _Not signed_, _Signing failed_, or _Not considered yet_), what has been paid (_Paid_, _Partly paid_, _Unpaid_, or _Credited_ when credit notes cover all of it) and any amount credited. Payment follows the order's payment status, which receipts keep up to date.
  • Open invoice opens the invoice as the document it is, in a large window over the list (closing it, with Close or Escape, returns to the list as it was). At the top: the customer, when it was issued and emailed, the link Open order, and the chips for kind, KRA signing, payment and Order waiting for approval. Under that four figures: Invoice total, Credited, Paid and Balance due (a proforma or delivery invoice shows no balance, and a part invoice shows its own total only). Then What was invoiced as a table with named columns: Item (with its code), Quantity (with its unit), Unit price (the price before a discount struck through when one was given), Discount, Tax and Line total; on a phone each line is a card with the same names. Under the table the sums: Before tax, Delivery, Tax, Total, the discount already taken off, Credit notes, Paid and Balance due. Then the credit notes against it (number, status, date, amount) and the signing log. Download PDF and Send again by email stay at the foot of the window wherever you scroll. An order the shop already records as paid shows as paid in full whatever the ledger shows.
  • Raise an invoice: choose an order to invoice (search by order number or customer) and press Raise invoice. Only orders with no tax invoice yet are offered, and not those waiting for or refused by approval, cancelled or failed. The invoice is for the whole order. The invoicing rules hold: a tax invoice cannot be raised while the order waits for approval, the number is gap-free per branch, and KRA signing never holds the invoice up. An order that already has one is refused in words.
  • New sales invoice (a direct sale): for a sale invoiced at once, with no sales order in front of it. Needs the _Sales invoices: create_ permission. The editor is the one for sales orders: choose the customer (the credit position shows, as the settings for sales invoices will look at it), add products and packages, the expected payment, the day needed, and Hold the stock until this invoice is paid where the company allows it, then Issue invoice. The server prices it and applies the company's Selling Documents settings for _Sales invoices_: by default it checks the credit limit (over it is refused in words), falls due on the customer's payment terms, makes the tax invoice with it and issues the stock at once; each of these is a setting (credit check, credit days, when stock is released, approval). The invoice is numbered from the fiscal tax-invoice series and signed under its own _Sales invoices_ KRA signing switch (set it in the KRA settings like the others). In the list it shows as _(direct sale)_. If an approval is needed it is issued waiting for approval; its tax invoice (and its stock, where it leaves when issued) follow automatically as soon as it is approved, unless the company turned _Invoice after approval_ off in Selling Documents, in which case staff use Raise an invoice once it is approved.
  • A signed invoice is never edited or deleted: it is corrected by a credit note (from the order's details). Raising an invoice for part of an order, or one invoice per delivery, is a later module (partial billing).

Who is written to, and which contacts a quote shows

The email staff send with Send via Email goes where Settings, Email Routing says for _Quote sent to the customer_: by default to the customer with replies to the company email, and it can be set to write to several people, copy the sender or others, blind-copy the manager and answer to a chosen address. The "Questions? Contact …" emails on the quote PDF, the public quote page and the email follow the company's setting for quotes made by staff, or for quotes asked for on the web shop. A single quote can override them: in the quote editor, Business contacts shown on this quote. A quote with no email for the customer can still be sent when Email Routing names other people to write to; if nobody can be found, the message says to add a customer email, and if the company switched quote emails off, it says so.

Packages on a Quote

  • A package line reads as its choices ("Express lunch: Large fish, Ugali and Sukuma") in the editor, the PDF and the email. The server works out the price, the tax (each chosen part at its own rate, like a kit) and the cost (what the chosen parts cost); the margin and the price floor use those figures.
  • The quote keeps the choices by the slot's name and the part, not by internal ids. A package changed after the quote was made does not stop the quote being understood; if a chosen part is no longer offered, converting the quote stops and names it ("Large fish is no longer offered in Fish"), the quote can be reopened, the part replaced and saved again. Stock is not looked at when quoting; it is looked at, with the package's ordering rules (servings, notice, closing time, days, daily limit, who may order) and the date in Needed On, when the quote becomes an order. The quote's price stands even if the package's base price has moved.
  • A note can be written on a package line of a quote when the package takes notes; it is kept with the line and goes on to the order and the preparation sheet.
  • Two lines of one package with different choices stay two lines, also on the order; the exact selection of each is saved with the order for the preparation sheet.

Stage Immutability & Reversals

  • Once an order stage timestamp is recorded in the append-only event log, it can never be edited or deleted.
  • If an order must be cancelled after dispatch:
  1. The order status moves to Delivery Failed or Cancelled.
  2. A return-to-stock movement is issued, recording the physical return of the goods to inventory.
  3. A credit note is generated referencing the original invoice.

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

StepVerification TaskExpected ResultPass/Fail
1Create a test Cash Customer and Credit Customer.Both customers saved; credit limit reflected on Credit Customer.[ ]
2Issue a Sales Quote with a 10% line discount.Proforma calculates discount and VAT accurately; status shows Draft/Sent.[ ]
3Convert Quote to Order.Order created with identical lines; Quote status transitions to Converted.[ ]
4Attempt to place an order exceeding Credit Customer's limit.System blocks or routes to Credit Approval queue as configured.[ ]
4bPlace two package orders for the same day, cancel one, open Preparation sheet for that day.Totals and each order's choices show for the kept order only; Print leaves out the menu.[ ]
4aIf the company sells packages: quote one with Add a package, change its choices, convert the quote.The line reads as its choices; the order's parts add up to the quote's total; a package with a daily limit refuses a second quote for the same date once full.[ ]
5Verify Order Timeline Events.Placement, payment, and dispatch timestamps render accurately in order modal.[ ]

chapters.htmlContent:
Guide 04: Pricing Engine, Promotions & Margins (/admin/pricing)

The Pricing Engine is the commercial brain of QSell. It governs how base prices are determined across different customer tiers, retail channels, and branches, while enforcing strict margin protection rules, promotional coupons, retrospective rebates, loyalty points, and role-based discount caps.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • Erosion of Profitability Through Uncontrolled Discounting: In competitive sales environments, sales reps frequently offer deep discounts to close deals, inadvertently selling products below cost or wiping out gross margin.
  • Accidental Discount Stacking: Businesses often run promotional coupons (e.g. 10% off) that unintentionally stack on top of existing wholesale volume discounts and loyalty redemptions, leading to crippling margin loss.
  • Complexity in Multi-Tier B2B Pricing: Managing different price sheets for retail customers, wholesale stockists, contractors, and export clients on paper or spreadsheets causes billing errors and client disputes.
  • No Explanation of How a Price Was Reached: When a customer asks "Why was I charged KES 1,850 instead of KES 1,700?", legacy ERPs cannot explain the calculation. QSell generates a deterministic Price Trace explaining every step in the waterfall.

Target Client Profiles

  • Wholesalers & FMCG Distributors: Utilizing customer tiers (Wholesale A/B/C), minimum order quantities (MOQs), and tiered volume breaks (e.g. 1-10 units @ KES 1,000; 11-50 units @ KES 920; 51+ units @ KES 850).
  • Multi-Branch Retailers: Charging localized prices based on branch geography or transport costs (e.g. Nairobi vs. Lodwar).
  • High-Margin Hardware & Contractor Suppliers: Requiring cost-plus minimum price floors to ensure every sale yields at least a 15% gross margin.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you will never accidentally sell a product at a loss again. Our pricing engine lets you configure sophisticated wholesale price lists, volume breaks, and seasonal promotional codes, while locking your bottom line with automated Price Floors. If a salesperson attempts to discount an item below your required margin floor, the system blocks the transaction or automatically routes it to the Managing Director for approval. Best of all, our Price Check simulator allows you to test any pricing rule before it goes live."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • 100% Margin Floor Lock: Hard stop prevents any quote or order from being sold below cost + minimum markup.
  • Deterministic Price Trace: Complete auditability on every transaction line item.
  • Controlled Discretionary Limits: Sales reps, supervisors, and managers each have defined discount authority ceilings.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    PROD[1. Products & Base Landed Costs Configured] --> GRP[2. Customer Groups Defined: Wholesale, Retail]
    GRP --> LIST[3. Price Lists Created with Scope & Validity]
    LIST --> FLOOR[4. Price Floors Set: Cost + Minimum %]
    FLOOR --> LIMIT[5. Staff Override Limits Assigned]
    LIMIT --> SIM[6. Price Check Simulator Verification]
  1. Product Master Data: SKUs must exist with valid Base Selling Prices and Unit Cost Prices under Catalog > Products.
  2. Customer Groups: Defined under /admin/pricing/groups (e.g. Retail Cash, Trade Tier 1, Government Tender).
  3. Price Lists: Created with currency (KES), validity dates, and branch/customer scope.
  4. Price Floors: Configured under /admin/pricing/floors to set non-negotiable minimum profit barriers.
  5. Override Limits: Configured under /admin/pricing/limits to set role-based discount authority.
  6. Required Permissions: pricing:read to view and pricing:manage to create or alter price rules.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Pricing Engine operates as a deterministic 2-phase calculation waterfall:

graph TD
    subgraph Phase1["Phase 1: Base Price Resolution (Choose Winner)"]
        IN[Inputs: Customer, Group, Branch, SKU, Qty, Date]
        IN --> MATCH[Match Active Price Sources]
        MATCH --> RANK[Rank by Specificity: Customer > Group > Branch > Standard]
        RANK --> PRIO[Break Ties: Priority > Newest Effective Date]
        PRIO --> BASE[Base Price Chosen]
    end

    subgraph Phase2["Phase 2: Adjustments & Safeguards (Stack & Check)"]
        BASE --> DISC[Apply Eligible Discounts & Coupons]
        DISC --> REB[Accrue Retrospective Rebates]
        REB --> PROMO[Evaluate Loyalty Points & Gift Cards]
        PROMO --> FLOOR{Check Price Floor: Price >= Cost + Min Margin?}
        FLOOR -- "Compliant" --> WIN[Effective Final Price]
        FLOOR -- "Breached" --> APP{Within Staff Override Limit?}
        APP -- "Yes" --> WARN[Flag Margin Warning & Allow]
        APP -- "No" --> BLOCK[Route to Approval / Block Sale]
    end

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Sub-Module 1: Customer Groups (/admin/pricing/groups)

  • Defines customer segmentation tiers (e.g., Walk-in Retail, Wholesale Bronze, Wholesale Platinum, Staff).
  • Allows assigning customers in bulk or binding automatic qualifying criteria.

Sub-Module 2: Price Lists (/admin/pricing)

  • Table of active and scheduled price lists showing Code, Name, Currency, Priority, Effective Dates, and Scope.
  • Line Editor: Set prices per SKU, Unit of Measure, and Quantity Breaks (e.g. Buy 10+, Buy 50+, Buy 100+).

Sub-Module 3: Discounts & Coupons (/admin/pricing/discounts)

  • Configures promotional campaigns:
  • Type: Percentage discount (e.g. 10% off), Fixed amount (e.g. KES 500 off), or Free Item.
  • Trigger: Coupon code entry, minimum cart value threshold (e.g. Spend KES 10,000+), or specific product bundles.
  • Stacking Rules: Whether this discount can combine with other active promotions.

Sub-Module 4: Rebates (/admin/pricing/rebates)

  • Long-term customer loyalty agreements:
  • Tracks cumulative purchase volume over a calendar quarter or year.
  • Accrues rebate percentages (e.g. "Buy KES 2,000,000 of cement in Q1, receive 3% credit rebate").
  • Automatically generates Accounts Receivable Credit Memos upon milestone attainment.

Sub-Module 5: Loyalty Points (/admin/pricing/loyalty)

  • Point accrual engine: Set earn rate (e.g. 1 Point per KES 100 spent) and redemption rate (e.g. 1 Point = KES 1.00 store credit).
  • Expiration rules and minimum points required to redeem.

Sub-Module 6: Gift Cards (/admin/pricing/gift-cards)

  • Prepaid voucher management: Generate digital gift card codes, assign balances, track partial redemptions, and monitor expiration dates.

Sub-Module 7: Price Book (/admin/pricing/book)

  • Printable and exportable matrix showing what every product sells for in any combination of Customer Group, Branch, and Quantity tier. Ideal for distributing physical price sheets to field sales agents.

Sub-Module 8: Pricing Insights (/admin/reports/pricing-insights)

  • Executive analytics dashboard displaying:
  • Average realized gross margin across all orders.
  • Total revenue surrendered to promotional discounts and coupon codes.
  • Frequency of manual price overrides by sales representatives.

Sub-Module 9: Price Floors (/admin/pricing/floors)

  • The ultimate margin defense system:
  • Configures minimum selling prices based on:
  • Cost + Percentage Markup (e.g. Cost + 15%).
  • Cost + Fixed Amount (e.g. Cost + KES 200).
  • Hard Absolute Price Floor (e.g. Never sell below KES 1,500).
  • Scoped by specific Product, Product Group, or Category.

Sub-Module 10: Override Limits (/admin/pricing/limits)

  • Governs how far a staff member may manually lower a price or apply a discretionary discount:
  • Junior Sales Rep: Max 3% discount, cannot breach price floor.
  • Senior Sales Account Manager: Max 10% discount.
  • Branch Manager: Max 18% discount.
  • Commercial Director: Unlimited override authority.

Sub-Module 11: Price Check / Simulator (/admin/pricing/check)

  • The interactive sandbox where implementors and sales reps can test pricing scenarios:
  • Input: Select a Customer, Branch, Product SKU, Quantity, and Date.
  • Output: Instant live calculation with full waterfall trace displaying every considered price list, why one won, and which discounts applied.

Sub-Module 12: Price Rules (/admin/pricing/rules)

  • Master resolution settings configuring the relative weights and specificity rankings of competing price sources.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

Price List Line & Quantity Break Fields (/admin/pricing/[id])

Field LabelPurposeType & FormatRequired?Validation Rules & Hints
Product / SKUTarget item being priced.Lookup AutocompleteRequiredMust be an active sellable product.
Unit of MeasureSelling package.DropdownRequirede.g. Piece, Box of 24, Kilogram.
Minimum QuantityTier threshold (From Qty).Integer / DecimalRequiredTier 1 begins at 1. Subsequent tiers must be higher.
Tier PriceUnit price for this quantity tier.Currency (KES)RequiredMust be $> 0$. Format: 2 decimal places.
Pricing MethodHow tier applies.Radio SelectorRequiredAll Units (retroactive to unit 1) or Incremental (bracketed).
Start DateEffective start date.Date (YYYY-MM-DD)OptionalIf blank, active immediately upon publishing.
End DateExpiration date.Date (YYYY-MM-DD)OptionalMust be $\ge$ Start Date. Automatically retires at 23:59:59.

Price Floor Fields (/admin/pricing/floors/new)

Field LabelPurposeType & FormatRequired?Validation Rules & Hints
Scope TypeLevel of floor application.DropdownRequiredCompany-Wide, Category, Product Group, Specific SKU.
Target EntitySelected category or product.Lookup AutocompleteRequired if not Company-WideSelects the entity to protect.
Floor MethodHow the minimum price is calculated.DropdownRequiredCost + Markup %, Cost + Fixed Amount, Fixed Minimum Price.
Floor ValueThe rate or amount.Decimal / CurrencyRequirede.g. 15.0 for 15% markup, or 250.00 for KES 250 margin.
EnforcementBehavior upon violation.Radio SelectorRequiredHard Stop (Block Sale) or Require Manager Approval.

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions (Down to the Last Click)

Action 1: Setting Up a Tiered Wholesale Price List

  1. Navigate to /admin/pricing and click New Price List.
  2. Enter List Name: "Wholesale Platinum Tier 1".
  3. Set Currency: KES.
  4. Set Scope: In the Customer Group dropdown, select "Wholesale Platinum".
  5. Set Priority: 10 (higher priority wins over generic lists).
  6. Click Save & Add Products.
  7. In the product lines table, click Add Product.
  8. Select the SKU (e.g., "Cement 50kg Bag").
  9. In Tier 1: Set From Qty: 1, Price: 750.00.
  10. Click Add Tier: Set From Qty: 50, Price: 710.00.
  11. Click Add Tier: Set From Qty: 200, Price: 680.00.
  12. Click Save Price List.
  13. Status updates to Active. Any Wholesale Platinum customer ordering 50+ bags instantly receives KES 710.00.

Action 2: Protecting Margins by Configuring a Price Floor

  1. Navigate to /admin/pricing/floors and click New Price Floor.
  2. Set Scope Type to Category.
  3. Select Category: "Power Tools & Machinery".
  4. Set Floor Method: Cost + Markup %.
  5. Enter Floor Value: 20.0 (meaning Cost + 20%).
  6. Set Enforcement: Hard Stop (Block Sale).
  7. Click Activate Price Floor.
  8. A green confirmation banner displays: "Price floor activated. 48 products protected." Any attempt to sell a power tool below cost + 20% is now impossible across all channels.

Action 3: Simulating a Transaction in the Price Check Sandbox

  1. Navigate to /admin/pricing/check.
  2. In the Customer lookup, select "QuickFix Contractors".
  3. In the Product lookup, select "Inverter 5kVA".
  4. In the Quantity box, type 5.
  5. In the Branch dropdown, select "Nairobi Westlands".
  6. Click the Simulate Price button.
  7. The Waterfall Trace displays:
  • Standard Retail Price: KES 120,000.00
  • Customer Group Match (Trade): KES 108,000.00 (Wins by Specificity)
  • Quantity Break (5+ units): KES 102,000.00
  • Active Coupon SAVE5: - KES 5,100.00 (Applied)
  • Price Floor Check: Landed Cost KES 85,000.00 + 15% Floor (KES 97,750.00).
  • Floor Result: PASS (Net KES 96,900 is below floor? Triggers warning/approval).
  1. The tool displays the exact formula and reason string that will be written to the order.

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

Specificity Hierarchy (Who Wins When Prices Compete?)

When multiple active price sources match an order line, the winner is determined strictly by the Specificity Hierarchy:

  1. Contract Locked Price (Explicit legal agreement with client).
  2. Customer-Specific Price (Negotiated price sheet for this single account).
  3. Customer Group Price (Tiered wholesale or trade group).
  4. Route / Van Price (Mobile distribution route).
  5. Branch / Location Price (Regional store price).
  6. Standard Product Price (Base catalog price).

Ties are broken by Price List Priority integer, then Newest Effective Date.

Preventing Coupon Cannibalization

  • If a discount has the flag allow_stacking = false, applying it disables all other promotional discounts on that order line.
  • The system automatically compares the single unstacked discount against the sum of competing stacked discounts and awards the customer the better of the two deals without double-dipping.

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

StepVerification TaskExpected ResultPass/Fail
1Create Customer Group "Wholesale" and assign a test customer.Customer profile reflects the new group.[ ]
2Create a Price List for Wholesale with quantity break at 10 units.Buying 9 units quotes Base Price; buying 10 units quotes Tier Price.[ ]
3Configure a 20% Cost-Plus Price Floor on a test product.Selling below Cost + 20% is blocked with explicit floor warning.[ ]
4Test Staff Override Limit for a Junior Sales Rep.Entering a manual discount above 5% is blocked.[ ]
5Run Price Check Simulator on 3 complex scenarios.Trace displays correct winning source, applied discounts, and margin check.[ ]

chapters.htmlContent:
Guide 05: Products Catalog & Inventory Control (/admin/catalog, /admin/inventory)

The Products & Inventory Control module governs the entire physical life of products—from SKU master definition and multi-level category classification to multi-location warehouse management, units of measure conversions, kits and hampers, two-step stock transfers, and continuous physical cycle counts.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • The "Single Stock Number" Blind Spot: In basic systems, a product has one global stock number (e.g. "50 units on hand"). Management has no idea if those 50 units are in the Nairobi central depot, the Mombasa branch, or on a rider's delivery van, leading to false promises to customers.
  • Lost Goods in Transit: Moving stock between warehouses or out on delivery vans is where theft and shrinkage occur. Traditional spreadsheets write off stock immediately upon dispatch, losing all accountability while goods are on the road. QSell introduces an In-Transit Ledger where goods remain on the company's books until formally acknowledged and received at the destination.
  • Stock Counts That Force Business Closures: Businesses often shut down operations for an entire weekend to conduct physical inventory counts. In QSell, Continuous Cycle Counting allows warehouse staff to count shelves while retail cashiers and the web shop continue selling without discrepancy errors.
  • Unit of Measure Confusion: Selling a product in pieces, 12-packs, and 24-box cartons typically causes inventory chaos. QSell enforces strict base-unit decimal conversions (e.g., kilograms, litres, pieces).

Target Client Profiles

  • Multi-Branch Retailers & Wholesalers: Operating central distribution hubs, regional branch stores, and mobile van-sales fleets.
  • Hardware, Agro-Dealers & Building Suppliers: Selling goods by weight, length, volume, or pack sizes (cement, paint, fertilizer, cabling).
  • Gift, Hamper & Food Distributors: Assembling multi-item gift hampers and combo kits priced as a single unit but fulfilled and taxed as individual components.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "With QSell, you always know exactly what you have, exactly where it sits, and what it is worth. Your inventory isn't just a number on a spreadsheet—it is an immutable ledger. You can see real-time stock across every warehouse, branch shop, and delivery van. When you move stock between locations, it is tracked in transit. And best of all, you can perform physical stock audits on your shelves during business hours while your cashiers keep ringing up sales."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • Zero Shrinkage in Transit: Two-step transfers require sender dispatch and receiver sign-off with variance reporting.
  • Zero Interrupted Trading: Continuous cycle counts eliminate the need for costly weekend store closures.
  • Kit Component Explosion: Bundles automatically deduct stock and calculate KRA tax for individual underlying components.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

graph TD
    UOM[1. Units of Measure: Pcs, Kg, Box Defined] --> CLAS[2. Business Classifications: Stocked, Service]
    CLAS --> LOC[3. Stock Locations Created: Warehouses, Stores, Vans]
    LOC --> CAT[4. Categories & Tax Classes Mapped]
    CAT --> PROD[5. SKUs & Kits Configured]
    PROD --> CUT[6. Stock Ledger Opening Balance Cutover]
  1. Units of Measure: Defined under /admin/settings/units (Base units and conversion multipliers).
  2. Business Classifications: Defined under /admin/item-types (Determining whether an item is physical stock, service, or consumable).
  3. Stock Locations: Defined under /admin/inventory/locations (At least one default warehouse or shop).
  4. Categories: Created under /admin/categories with mapped KRA tax classifications.
  5. Staff Permissions:
  • products:read, products:manage: Create and manage catalog SKUs.
  • stock:read, stock:manage: View stock levels, issue transfers, and conduct counts.
  • stock:cutover: Execute initial opening balance migration.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

The Products & Inventory module is divided into two operational domains:

graph TD
    subgraph CatalogDomain["Catalog Definition (/admin/catalog)"]
        PROD["Products Master & SKUs"]
        CAT["Category Hierarchy"]
        CLAS["Business Classifications"]
        UOM["Units of Measure & Decimals"]
        KITS["Kits & Hampers (Bundles)"]
    end

    subgraph InventoryDomain["Warehouse Management (/admin/inventory)"]
        LOC["Stock Locations (Depot, Shop, Van)"]
        BAL["Stock Balances: On-Hand vs Reserved"]
        TRANS["Stock Transfers & In-Transit"]
        COUNTS["Physical Cycle Counts & Audits"]
        LEDGER["Immutable Stock Ledger"]
    end

    CatalogDomain --> InventoryDomain

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Sub-Module 1: Products Master (/admin/products)

  • Product Directory: Server-paged table with instant filtering by Category, Stock Status (In Stock, Low Stock, Out of Stock), Classification, and Channel visibility.
  • Product Editor (/admin/products/[id]):
  • Basic Info: Title, SKU, Barcode (EAN-13/UPC), Brand, Category, Short Description, and HTML Rich-Text Body.
  • Pricing & Tax: Selling Price, Cost Price (for gross margin calculation), KRA Tax Classification (16% VAT, Zero-Rated, Exempt).
  • Stock & Units: Unit of Measure picker, Minimum Reorder Threshold, Safety Stock, and Track Inventory toggle.
  • Web Shop Flags: Show on Web Shop toggle, Sold only inside packages toggle, SEO title/description, and high-resolution gallery image uploader.

Sub-Module 2: Trash (/admin/trash/products)

  • Soft-delete recovery screen. Products removed from the catalog can be Restored as Drafts or permanently purged (only if no historic transaction or stock ledger records exist).

Sub-Module 3: Business Classifications (/admin/item-types)

  • Establishes product accounting behavior:
  • Stocked Goods: Physical inventory tracked in warehouses.
  • Non-Stocked Services: Labor, installation, delivery fees, consulting.
  • Consumables / Packaging: Boxes, tape, branded bags used at checkout.
  • Controls whether the item is "Sold to Customers" across quotes, orders, and storefront.

Sub-Module 4: Units of Measure (/admin/settings/units)

  • Global table of measurement units (e.g., PCS, KG, LTR, BOX, MTR).
  • Enforces decimal precision (e.g. Kilograms allow 3 decimals 1.425 kg, while Pieces allow 0 decimals 1 pc).
  • Defines conversion ratios (e.g., 1 Box = 24 Pieces).

Sub-Module 5: Categories (/admin/categories)

  • Multi-level tree view for organizing products into departments, categories, and subcategories. Drives storefront mega-menus and automated KRA tax inheritance.

Sub-Module 6: Kits and Hampers (/admin/pricing/kits)

  • Bundle creator: Defines combo packages (e.g., "Solar Home Kit 1kVA" or "Executive Christmas Hamper").
  • Line component mapping: Links 4 individual panels, 1 inverter, 2 batteries, and 1 mounting kit into a single sellable SKU.
  • Component Tax Handling: Automatically apportions VAT across components with differing tax rates.

Sub-Module 6A: Packages (/admin/pricing/packages)

A package is one product made of choices, for a business whose customers build what they buy: a lunch with a fish, a starch and vegetables to pick; a computer set with a choice of memory, storage and screen. A kit is always the same parts; a package lets the shopper decide some of them. Permission: pricing read to see, pricing manage to make, change or remove. Every change needs a reason from the pricing reasons list and is written to the decision log.

What you set up, in order

  1. Make the parts as ordinary stock products. A part that nobody should buy alone (brown ugali, a side portion) is marked Sold only inside packages on its product; it keeps its stock, cost and tax but is not listed, found or sold by itself.
  2. Make the package product (for example Express lunch) with its base price. It must be sold to customers; it cannot be a kit, a part of a kit, a part of another package or marked sold only inside packages.
  3. On the Packages screen choose New package, pick that product and set:
  • How the package is priced: one base price plus a difference for each option (the usual), or each option priced on its own and added up.
  • How the price is split over the parts (for the tax and stock lines on the order): in proportion to the parts' prices (usual), their cost, or shares you set.
  • An option that is out of stock: hide it (usual), show it greyed out saying it is sold out, or show it greyed out and suggest another.
  • In use: when off, the product sells as an ordinary product.
  1. Add slots, one for each decision (Fish, Starch, Vegetables, Extras). For each slot give the fewest and most picks (1 and 1 is a single choice; 0 as the fewest makes it optional; 1 and 2 lets the shopper pick one or two), whether the same option can be chosen more than once (extra portions), and whether it is included, not a choice (one option that is always part of it).
  2. Add options to each slot: the product, the quantity of it in one pick, a difference to the base price (zero, higher or lower; in base plus differences mode) or a fixed price (in summed mode; empty means the product's own selling price), and whether it is pre-selected.
  3. Choose a reason and Save package. The change applies to the next order; orders already made keep what was chosen.

Rules the screen enforces (the server checks them again): the fewest servings is not more than the most, closing needs a time of day, a group audience needs at least one group; at least one slot (at most 20) with at least one option (at most 50); the fewest picks is not more than the most; the same product is not listed twice in a slot; a package cannot contain itself, a kit or another package; every product must exist and be sold to customers; in summed mode every option needs a price; with shares you set every option needs a share. The package list shows the "from" price (the cheapest valid choice), warns in red when that choice sells below what its parts cost, and flags options that can no longer be chosen because their product was switched off or deleted. Pricing → Insights raises the same two warnings.

Protection: a product that a package offers cannot be deleted (switch it off, or take it out of the package first). Removing a package does not touch orders or quotes already made.

Slots filled from a category, a note on each serving, and order again

  • Where a slot's options come from: for each slot choose a list I make, product by product (the usual) or every product of a category. With a category, every product of it that can be sold (switched on, sold to customers, not checkout packaging, not a kit, not a package, not the package itself) is an option, up to 100 by name, so a vegetable added to the category later appears on the package by itself. Set once for the slot: the category, the quantity of each pick and the difference to the base price (or, in summed pricing, a fixed price; empty means each product's own selling price). A category slot cannot be an included slot, and shares you set (the split by shares) cannot be used with it: split by price or by cost. Saving is refused for a category that does not exist or has nothing that can be sold in a package. A category cannot be deleted while a package slot uses it.
  • Customers can write a note on each serving (a setting on the package, off until turned on): a box under the builder, up to 200 characters, kept with the cart line and the order and shown on the preparation sheet ("Note: no pepper") and in the quote. The note is plain text, never markup. The same choices with another note are another line. A package that does not take notes refuses one.
  • Order again: a signed-in shopper opening a package sees their own earlier selections of it (newest first, each once, up to three) with the servings, the note and today's price, and Add again puts one in the cart. Each earlier choice is found again by slot and part against today's package and stock. A part that is sold out today is swapped for the nearest available option of the same slot (the first available one), and the card says so ("Cabbage instead of Sukuma, which is sold out today"); a selection that cannot be made today at all is not offered. The server checks it again when it is added, like anything else. A signed-out visitor sees none.

How shoppers order a package: Add to cart, Request a quote, or either (a setting on each package)

  • In Pricing → Packages, open a package (Change …) and choose How shoppers order it on the web shop: Add to cart and pay at checkout (the usual, and what every existing package keeps), Request a quote only: we send the price first, or Either: the shopper chooses Add to cart or Request a quote. The list shows a chip (Quote request only or Cart or quote request) for packages that are not cart-only. Saving needs a reason like every package change, and the change applies to the next visitor.
  • Request a quote only (for corporate, event and large-group packages whose price and terms you agree first): the package page shows Request a quote and no Add to cart, Buy now, Order for a group or Order again. Every option is shown even when stock is short, because a quote promises nothing from the shelves; stock is checked when the quote becomes an order.
  • Either shows Add to cart and Buy now as before with Request a quote beside them.
  • What the shopper does: builds the package as usual (the price moves with each choice), presses Request a quote, and fills in a short form: name, email, phone (an email address or a phone number is needed so you can answer), Needed on (optional) and Anything we should know (optional). A signed-in shopper's details are filled in from their account. They see We have your request: quote … with the quote number. The request is limited per visitor and per email or phone, so nobody can fill your quote list.
  • What you see: a new quote in Sales Quotes, a draft priced from the package as it is now (the shopper's browser never sets a price), with the customer's details, the date it is needed, their message in the internal notes, and Requested on the web shop shown where Created by normally is. Check or adjust it, Send via Email, and when the customer accepts it through their link it converts to an order as any quote does; the order is allowed even though the package is quote-only, because staff documents are not the cart.
  • Rules: a package that is Add-to-cart only refuses a quote request; a quote-only package refuses the cart at checkout and at the basket check, and refuses to start a group order, each with a plain message. Rules of ordering (notice, closing time, daily limit, who may order) are applied when the quote becomes an order, not when it is requested. Two mails go out when a request is made, queued so a mail server that is down only delays them. Who they go to is set in Settings, Email Routing (several staff, Cc, Bcc, Reply-To; by default the company's own email address for the alert and the shopper for the confirmation). The alert says who asked, how to reach them, what was asked for, the date and what they wrote, with a link to Sales Quotes; and, when the shopper gave an email address, a confirmation to the shopper with their request number, what they asked for and the price as it stands, saying nothing is ordered or charged until they accept. A shopper who gave only a phone number gets no confirmation (unless Email Routing names others for it), so call them. If nobody can be found for the alert (no company email and nobody chosen), none is sent. Signed-in shoppers also see their requests in My account, My quote requests, with where each stands (Being prepared, Sent to you, Accepted with the order, Declined, Expired, Cancelled).

Group orders (a link where each person chooses their own, and one person pays)

  • On any package's page a signed-in shopper can press Order for a group, optionally say what it is for, the date it is needed and the time by which people must choose, and Start the group order. They land on the group's page, which has a link to share (a long unguessable address, kept only as a one-way fingerprint) and a Copy link button. A signed-out visitor is asked to sign in first. One organiser can have at most 20 open group orders.
  • Anyone with the link (no account needed) opens /group/…, sees the title, who is organising, the package, the date and the closing time, types their name, and chooses one serving with the same builder as the shop (no servings control; the note box reads "Anything the kitchen should know" where the package takes notes). The choice is checked like an order's: the package as it is today, the choices, the note and stock for a serving. They are told Your choice is saved. Their browser remembers it, so reopening the link shows Your choice, with Change my choice and Withdraw my choice (asks first). Nobody can change or withdraw anyone else's: each choice has a secret that only that browser holds (kept only as a fingerprint on the server). Up to 100 people per group order.
  • The organiser's page shows, to the organiser only, who has chosen what with each note, and lets them remove anyone's choice (asks first), stop taking choices, take choices again, or cancel the group order. Everyone else sees only how many people have chosen. A visitor who opens the link after the closing time, after the organiser stopped it, or after it was cancelled is told so in words and cannot choose.
  • Put everyone's lunch in my cart puts the choices in the organiser's cart as ordinary package lines: identical choices (same options, same note) become one line with that many servings. The group is then closed to new choices. A person whose choice can no longer be made today (a part sold out or taken out of the package) is named, not dropped, with the reason, so the organiser can sort it out with them (reopen the group, or order that lunch separately). The organiser then checks out once and pays once: the order is an ordinary order, so the package's ordering rules (fewest servings, notice, daily limit, who may order), stock, price and the preparation sheet all apply as to any order.
  • The group's page is not indexed by search engines and is left out of the sitemap; opening links and choosing are rate limited per visitor and per link.
  • The order is tied back to the group. When the organiser places the order with the lines that came from the group, the group is marked ordered with the order number and the time, and the group's page says You ordered this group as order … with a link to My orders. From then on it cannot be put in the cart again, opened again or cancelled (it is done), so the same lunches are never paid for twice. Only the organiser's own order counts: another customer's order that names the group, a cancelled group, or an address that is not a group changes nothing and the order is placed as usual.
  • My group orders (account → My group orders, /profile/groups): the organiser's groups, newest first, each with its title or package, the date, how many people have chosen, its state (Taking choices, Closed, Ordered, Cancelled), the order number and a link to the order when there is one, and Open this group to get back to the page with the link, the choices and the cart button. The link is kept sealed under the shop's data key so it can be shown again; a group made before this was added, or while no data key was set, says The link for this group was not kept. A signed-out visitor is asked to sign in.
  • Not built yet: a reminder to people who have not chosen (the shop does not know who was invited, only who has chosen, so there is nobody to remind; the organiser shares the link again from the group's page).

What the shopper sees (the web shop builder)

  • A package is an ordinary product page with a step-by-step builder in place of the quantity box: one group for each slot, the rule in words ("Choose 1", "Choose 1 to 2", "Choose up to 2 (optional)", "Included"), the pre-selected options already chosen, and on every option card what it adds ("+ KES 120", "Included", "− KES 20", or its own price in summed mode). A slot with one pick is a set of round buttons (choose another to replace); a slot with several picks is a set of tick boxes, with + / − on an option when the same one may be chosen more than once.
  • The price is live: it moves with every choice and shows the total for the servings chosen ("KES 660 each for 2"). Servings have their own + / − (1 to 1,000).
  • Add to cart and Buy now are off until the choices are valid, and the reason is written next to them ("Choose an option for Vegetables."). One tap adds when the pre-selected options already make a valid choice.
  • Stock is read for all the servings, not one at a time. What the shop shows follows the package's option out of stock setting: hidden (nothing to choose, no dead end), greyed out saying "Sold out today", or greyed out with a one-tap "Try ..." suggestion. If a slot that needs a choice has nothing left, the package shows "not available right now" instead of a form. Two lunches asking for the last portion of ugali are refused while the shopper builds, naming the part ("Ugali is sold out for 4 servings."). Parts that are services or not counted never run out.
  • The cart line reads as a sentence: "Express lunch: Large fish, Ugali, Sukuma and Cabbage", with its price, a servings counter, Edit (reopens the builder with the choices kept and saves over the line) and Remove. The same choices are one line with more servings; different choices are different lines. The line is kept in the shopper's browser as choices only, never prices; on opening the cart, and after every change, the shop prices and checks it again and says plainly what is wrong (a part sold out, a choice removed from the package).
  • Product cards and listings show Choose options instead of Add and Buy now, so a package is never put in the cart as it stands. The package page does not show the product's own price (the builder shows the live one).
  • Security: the browser sends only product, option and slot ids and counts. Prices, quantities, tax and which options exist are all decided on the server; a choice from another package, a missing or duplicated option, too many or too few picks, a negative or fractional count, a package that is switched off or not sold on the web, or more than 20 package lines in one cart is refused with a plain message.

Rules of ordering (set per package on the Packages screen; empty means no rule)

  • Fewest and most servings per order (a group lunch from 10 servings), counted over all lines of one package in the order.
  • Notice needed (hours), ordering closes (a number of days before the date, at a time of day) and days it can be served (none ticked means every day), all counted in the company's time zone against the date the order is for.
  • Most servings promised for one day. The count is of orders that still stand (a cancelled order gives its servings back). Two orders for the last servings arrive at the same moment: the database queues them and one is told "Only 2 servings left for that date" or "fully booked", with no stock held for it.
  • Who may order: anyone, signed-in customers only, or only customers in the groups you choose. Group and corporate prices are not a setting here: they come from the price lists of those groups, which price the package product as they price any product. A different offer for a different audience is simply another package.
  • The date an order is for is the delivery time the shopper chose. A package with notice, closing, day or daily-limit rules asks for it; with none, the shopper is told "choose the date you need it". Notice is counted to the start of the chosen day. A staff channel without a delivery passes the date itself.
  • Every refusal says the rule in plain words and is kept on the checkout's record with its time and a reason ("Package ordering rule" or "Package choice problem").

What happens when a package is ordered

  1. The shop re-reads the package, checks every choice, prices it again (the base price through the price lists for that customer, plus what the choices add; or the choices' own prices added up) and checks stock for all the servings together. Nothing the browser says about price is used.
  2. Promotions and coupons apply to the package line like any line; then the price is shared over the chosen parts by the package's split method, each part taxed at its own product's rate, exactly like a kit. Parts of the same product that also appear elsewhere in the order fold into one line, so invoices, returns and credit notes work product by product. The order lines read "Large fish (Express lunch)".
  3. The choice actually made must not sell for less than its parts cost; otherwise the order is refused ("would sell for less than its parts cost").
  4. Stock is held for each part (never for the package product), in the same step as for any order. A cancelled order gives each part back; a return or credit note of one part credits that part's share.
  5. The exact selection is saved with the order (the package and its version, servings, price after discounts, the date, and every pick with its slot and the part's name as it was). This record, not the folded lines, says what to prepare, and it survives a later change or removal of the package.
  6. A package product added as a plain item (for example from an old saved cart) is refused.

On the shop: the package card and the package's structured data and share card show the from price (the cheapest valid choice). The checkout lists each package line with its price and the cart badge counts servings.

Preparation sheet: what to make for a day, from the choices saved with each order, with totals and print: Sub-Module 2A of guide 03 (/admin/orders/preparation).

Quotes and staff orders: a package can be sold on a quote with Add a package (guide 03) using the same builder, kept by slot name and part, converted to an order whose price stands, with a part the package no longer offers named and the conversion stopped. The documents that can sell a package are listed in one registry (web shop and staff orders, quotes); the point of sale, sales orders, sales invoices and credit sales are added to it when they are built, and a shared test runs the same package cases (same price, same tax, same parts, same refusals) against every registered document type.

What is not built yet (later slices): Request a quote instead of Add to cart; a package offered only on some channels; staff taking a package order directly (there is no staff order screen other than quotes yet); point of sale, sales orders, invoices and credit sales (they register themselves when built). A signed-in shopper's package lines are kept in the browser, not on the account yet. Notice is counted to the start of the day, not to a delivery slot's start time. The package's price does not yet go through option-by-option price lists (an option is charged at its product's selling price or the fixed price given). The package is already defined once and will be sold the same way everywhere.

Go-live check: make a package of two slots, open its page in the shop and confirm each choice moves the price as you expect, add it to the cart and edit it there, set an option's stock to zero and confirm it is hidden (or greyed out, per the setting), confirm the "from" price is what you expect, make the cheapest choice cost more than its parts, and confirm the red warning disappears. Switch one option's product off and confirm it is flagged.

Sub-Module 7: Stock Locations (/admin/inventory/locations)

  • Defines physical locations:
  • Warehouses: Central distribution godowns.
  • Retail Stores: Front-office shops where point-of-sale orders draw inventory.
  • Delivery Vans: Mobile stock locations assigned to riders for run dispatch.
  • Quarantine / Damaged: Holding locations for defective customer returns.

Sub-Module 8: Stock by Location (/admin/inventory/by-location)

  • Real-time stock matrix displaying product rows across location columns, showing:
  • On-Hand: Total physical units on shelves.
  • Reserved: Units committed to active customer orders awaiting dispatch.
  • Available: Uncommitted stock available to promise (On-Hand - Reserved).

Sub-Module 9: Stock Transfers (/admin/inventory/transfers)

  • Two-step inter-location workflow:
  1. Dispatch Transfer: Source location picks and dispatches goods. Stock moves from source On-Hand to In-Transit.
  2. Receive Transfer: Destination location inspects physical delivery and accepts goods. Stock moves from In-Transit to destination On-Hand.
  3. Discrepancy Reporting: Records damaged or missing items during transit.

Sub-Module 10: Stock Counts (/admin/inventory/counts)

  • Cycle counting engine:
  • Create a count session for a specific warehouse, aisle, or category.
  • Staff scan barcodes and record physical counts on mobile or desktop.
  • System freezes an inventory snapshot at count initiation: Cashiers keep selling!
  • Reconciliation view highlights positive/negative variances with KES financial impact.
  • Manager approves count, posting adjustment entries to the stock ledger.

Sub-Module 11: Stock Ledger & Cutover (/admin/inventory/ledger)

  • The single source of truth: An immutable, append-only log of every physical movement (receipts, sales dispatches, transfers, adjustments, returns, write-offs).
  • Includes the Cutover Wizard used during client onboarding to import verified opening inventory balances.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

Product SKU Master Fields (/admin/products/new)

Empty means not known: the product counts as nothing on a run. Once set it can be changed but not emptied from this form (as with the shipping weight). Not part of the CSV import.

Show on Web Shop is switched off for it and cannot be turned on. Needs a sellable item type and a selling price so a package can price it. Cannot be combined with checkout packaging. Turning it Off later does not put the product back in the shop: switch Show on Web Shop on again if you want that.
