chapters.htmlContent:
Guide 15: Reports & Analytics (/admin/reports, /admin)

The Reports module is where QSell shows owners and managers what the business is doing and whether they can trust the numbers. It has one front door (the Reports page), one design (the same charts, tables, period bar and download buttons on every report), and one rule: every figure is defined once, says which period and which branches it covers, and says when it was made. This guide covers the first release (the "foundation"): the Reports page, the Business Overview, the generic report page with downloads, the activity trail and the style guide. Budgets, targets, the tax suite and HR reports are planned in later releases and are not yet in the product.

---

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • "Which report do I open?" Reports are scattered across Finance, Vendors, Delivery and Customers. The Reports page lists every report the signed-in person may open, grouped by what it tells them, and searches by the question they have ("who owes us money?") and not only by report name.
  • Numbers that do not agree between screens. A figure such as "sales" or "owed by customers" has one definition used by every report. Receivable and payable reports are defined against their ledger control accounts.
  • Reports nobody can audit. Every download is recorded with who took it, when, in what format and a fingerprint of the file, so a file that was changed afterwards can be spotted.
  • Staff seeing figures they should not. Each report checks the person's permissions on the server before any figure is read. A person with no permission is told the report does not exist.
  • Spreadsheet trouble. Downloads open in Excel with correct characters, and any cell that could run a formula is neutralised.

Target Client Profiles

  • Owners and general managers who want a daily picture without learning each module.
  • Finance controllers who need downloadable, auditable ageing and ledger reports.
  • Multi-branch retailers and distributors who compare branches and periods.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "Open one page and every report you are allowed to see is there, in plain words: who owes you money, what you owe, how sales are moving. Every number says which dates and which branches it covers and when it was made. Download it to Excel or PDF and the system keeps a record of who took it. No more arguing over whose spreadsheet is right."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

  • Faster month-end: ageing reports download in one click instead of being rebuilt in spreadsheets.
  • Fewer disputes: one definition per figure, with the period and branch always stated.
  • Control: downloads are permissioned and audited; the audit trail cannot be edited or deleted.

---

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

  1. Roles and permissions (Guide 07). Grant the report permissions below to the right people. Nothing is open by default except to the administrator role.
  2. Source data. A report is only as useful as the module behind it: sales and payments (Guides 03, 11), customer ledgers and vendor ledgers (Guides 09, 10), branches (Guide 13).
  3. Branches. The branch picker lists the company's branches; someone without the all-branches permission sees only their own branches.
  4. Business time zone and currency (Guide 13). Periods such as "Today" follow the business's own days, not the server's.
PermissionWhat it allows
reports:readOpen the Reports page and the style guide.
reports:exportDownload a report as CSV, Excel or PDF.
reports:view_auditOpen Report activity (who ran and downloaded what).
reports:all_branchesChoose any branch in the branch picker, or see all branches together.
Each report's own permission (for example receivables_ageing:read)Open that report. A person needs it as well as reports:read.
dashboard:readOpen the Business Overview at /admin.

---

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

Mental model. A measure is one defined number (for example "Owed by customers"). A report is a set of measures broken down by dimensions (customer, branch, product…). Reports sit in families (Finance, Sales, Delivery and logistics…) so the Reports page can group them.

PartWherePurpose
Reports page/admin/reportsFind and open any report; star favourites.
Generic report page/admin/reports/<report>Shows a report with the period bar, a table and download buttons.
Existing screenstheir own addressesReports built earlier (for example vendor reports) keep their own screens; the Reports page links to them.
Business Overview/adminThe owner's daily summary.
Report activity/admin/reports/activityThe audit trail of runs and downloads.
Style guide/admin/reports/style-guideEvery chart and table in light and dark, for implementors and designers.

Upstream: sales, payments, customer and vendor ledgers, the general ledger. Downstream: none yet; budgets and targets will feed reports in later releases.

Freshness. Every report reads the live records. Each one shows when it was last updated: in the period bar, or under the title for reports about stock as it is now. Faster summaries and closed-period snapshots are planned and will say so on the report.

Where reports are. Every report opens under /admin/reports/<name>, and the Reports menu groups them by module: Sales, Point of sale and cash, Products and inventory, Finance, Customers, Vendors and purchasing, Delivery and logistics. A module's own link opens the Reports page narrowed to that module. The menu is built from the report list, so a new report appears in it, in the right module, as soon as it is registered. Reports that used to sit in other modules now live here only: Trial balance, Receivables ageing, Vendor reports, Vendor scorecards, Delivery report, Delivery performance, Late deliveries, Pricing insights and Customer analytics. The old addresses still work and send the person to the new one. Working screens that are not reports (journals, ledger entries, refunds, bank accounts and statements, till shifts, the price book) stay in their own modules.

---

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

4.1 Reports page (/admin/reports)

  • Find a report… button (Ctrl K / Cmd K). Opens a search box. Type a word such as "debtors"; use the arrow keys and Enter to open a result; Escape closes it.
  • Filter this list. Narrows the cards on the page as you type; matches the title, the question the report answers, keywords and the family.
  • Starred group. Reports you have starred appear first. Stars are kept in this browser only.
  • Family groups. Reports grouped under headings such as Finance or Delivery and logistics.
  • Report card. Shows the title, the question it answers, a star button and a link. The Business Overview is the home screen and is not listed here. A report that can be downloaded also has an "Open with downloads" link.
  • States. While loading, a placeholder is shown. If the person may open no report, a sentence says so and to ask an administrator. If the list fails to load, a message says so without technical detail.

4.2 Generic report page (/admin/reports/<report>)

  • A Back button at the top. It returns to the page the person came from (the Business Overview, the list, another report); a report opened directly goes back to the Reports list.
  • The report title, with the download buttons beside it.
  • The period and scope bar (see 4.4), where the report uses a period.
  • A table (cards on a phone; a sortable table from tablet width).
  • Download buttons (CSV, Excel, PDF) for the formats the report offers.
  • Reports that have their own screen and offer no downloads send the person straight to that screen.

4.3 Business Overview (/admin)

Headline figures with change against the comparison period, a sales trend chart, money collected, gross profit, owed by customers, stock health and an attention list. Each panel loads on its own, so a slow panel never holds up the others; a panel that fails says so and the rest still show.

4.4 Period and scope bar

  • Period buttons (for example Today, This month) and a From / To date pair for a custom range.
  • Compare choice: Previous period or Same period last year.
  • Branch picker (only for people who may choose a branch): a searchable list, never a drop-down menu.
  • Statement line: the dates covered, the comparison dates, the scope ("All branches" or the branch name) and "Updated" with the time the figures were made.

4.4a Downloaded files: heading, contents and names

  • File name. Every download is named <business>_<report>_<date>-<time>, for example sm-engineering-limited_stock-valuation_20261125-041300.pdf. The business is the trading name, the time is the business time zone to the second, and the same pattern applies to CSV, Excel and PDF, so files sort by when they were made.
  • PDF page one opens with the business name, then whatever the company chose to show under it (see Report headings below), then the report name, the question it answers, and one line saying what it covers: the days of the period, or "As at" a date and time for a report of a position (stock), followed by the branch or locations.
  • PDF table. Rows grow to fit long product or customer names, so nothing is cut off or printed over the next row. Numbers are grouped in thousands, money has two decimals, percentages carry the sign, and the heading row repeats on every page.
  • PDF footer. Business name, report name, when it was printed, and the page number. The internal definitions version is not printed; CSV and Excel keep it, with the as-of time, in their closing rows and Details sheet.
  • Report headings (/admin/settings/reports, needs the Company & Settings permission). The default is the business name only, as before. All reports (/admin/settings/reports/general) has eight switches: Logo, Registered name (when different from the trading name), Tagline, Address, Email, Phone numbers, Website and KRA PIN, with a preview built from the company's own details and two presets (Standard letterhead: logo, registered name, address, email and phone; Business name only). Each module of reports (Sales, Finance, Products and inventory and so on, one screen each under Settings → Reports) follows the general heading until Use the heading of all reports is unticked; it then keeps its own choice, and ticking the box again removes it. A detail the company profile does not hold is flagged beside its switch and is simply left off the page.

4.5 Report activity (/admin/reports/activity)

A list of runs and downloads: who, which report, when, format and the file fingerprint. Newest first; more rows load on request.

4.6 Style guide (/admin/reports/style-guide)

Examples of every chart (line, bars, stacked bars, ranked list, donut, target bar) and the table, each with a data table behind it. For implementors checking the look in light and dark mode and on a phone.

---

5. Granular Field-by-Field Reference

FieldWhereType and formatDefaultRequired
PeriodPeriod barOne of the preset buttons or CustomThe report's default (usually this month)Yes
FromPeriod barDate, YYYY-MM-DDStart of the periodOnly for Custom
ToPeriod barDate, YYYY-MM-DDEnd of the periodOnly for Custom
ComparePeriod barPrevious period / Same period last yearPrevious periodNo
BranchPeriod barSearch and pick a branchAll branches the person may seeNo
Filter this listReports pageFree textEmptyNo
FormatDownload buttonsCSV, Excel (.xlsx) or PDFn/aYes (by choosing a button)

Money is shown with the currency and thousands separators (for example KES 12,500). Percentages and changes are written in words as well as colour ("up 12.5% on the previous period").

---

6. Step-by-Step User Actions

Open a report. Reports → click the card, or press Ctrl K, type, Enter.

Star a report. Press the star on its card; it moves to the Starred group. Press it again to remove it. Stars stay in this browser only; a different browser or device starts with none.

Change the period. Click a period button; the page reloads the figures for that period and the address records the choice, so the link can be shared. For dates of your own, type From and To. If From is after To, the page says "The start date must be on or before the end date." and changes nothing.

Compare. Choose Previous period or Same period last year; the comparison dates are stated beside the period.

Pick a branch. Open the branch picker, type part of the name, choose. Choose "All branches" to clear it.

Download. Open the report's page and press CSV, Excel or PDF. The file is made on the spot and a record is added to Report activity. If the report is too long to download in full, the buttons are replaced by "Narrow the report to download it."; narrow the period or branch and try again.

See who downloaded what. Reports → Report activity (needs reports:view_audit).

---

7. Conditions, Business Rules & Edge Cases

  • Permission first. A report's permission is checked on the server before any figure is read. A report the person may not open is reported as not found, not as forbidden.
  • Branch limits. Without reports:all_branches a person only ever sees their own branches; a branch id typed into the address that they may not use is ignored.
  • Downloads. Need reports:export and the report's own permission. Only the formats a report offers are available. A long list that was cut short cannot be downloaded, so a file never silently lacks rows.
  • Spreadsheet safety. A cell that starts with =, +, - or @ is made harmless so Excel cannot run it. CSV files carry a marker so Excel reads accents and symbols correctly.
  • Audit. Every run of an audited report and every download is recorded before the file is returned. Records cannot be changed or deleted, even by an administrator.
  • File fingerprint. The fingerprint (SHA-256) is shown in the download's response and recorded with the entry, so a file's origin can be checked later.
  • Signed-in only. A download address opened without signing in answers "Please sign in again."
  • Tie-out. Receivable and payable ageing reports are designed to agree with their control accounts in the ledger (the report records which account). Automatic on-screen reconciliation of the two is planned for a later release.
  • Period notice. If a period was adjusted (for example a future end date was cut to today), a notice on the overview says so.
  • Fresh data. Every report says when it was updated; a figure is never shown without that.
  • No stored files. Downloaded files are not kept on the server.
  • Language. English only in this release; wording is held in one message catalogue so other languages can be added later without changing the reports.

---

8. Implementor Checklist & Go-Live Verification

Checklist

  1. Grant reports:read to the people who should see the Reports page, and dashboard:read for the Business Overview.
  2. Grant reports:export only to people who may take data out of the system.
  3. Grant reports:view_audit to the owner or finance controller only.
  4. Grant reports:all_branches to head-office staff; leave branch managers without it.
  5. Confirm the business time zone and base currency (Guide 13).
  6. Confirm each report's own permission is given to the right role (for example receivables_ageing:read).
  7. Fill in the company profile (name, logo, address, email, phone) and choose the report heading under Settings → Reports.

Test transactions

  1. Sign in as a branch manager. Open Reports: only permitted reports appear. The branch picker is absent or limited to their branches.
  2. Sign in as the owner. Open the Business Overview; switch to Today, then to Same period last year. The statement line changes dates and the address updates.
  3. Type From later than To; confirm the sentence refusing it and that nothing changes.
  4. Open Receivables ageing, download CSV, Excel and PDF. Open the CSV in Excel: accents are right and no cell starts with a formula.
  5. Open Report activity: three entries with your name, format and fingerprint.
  6. Sign in as someone without reports:export: the download is refused.
  7. On a phone (390 px wide): no sideways scrolling; tables appear as cards.
  8. Under Settings → Reports → All reports choose Standard letterhead, save, and download Stock valuation as a PDF: the business name, logo, address, email and phone sit above the report name, no row is cut off, and the file is named business, report and time.

Common pitfalls

  • Giving reports:read without the report's own permission: the card is hidden or the report reports as missing.
  • Expecting stars to follow the person to another device: they are per browser.
  • Expecting a closed-period snapshot or a budget comparison: not in this release.
  • Giving reports:export widely: every download is audited, but the data has left the system.

---

9. Report-by-Report Reference

Every report below opens from Reports (/admin/reports) and from the Business Overview's See the full report links, shows the period bar (period, comparison, branch), headline figures, one or two charts, a table, and notes saying what is counted. Each can be downloaded as CSV, Excel or PDF by someone who holds the download permission. A person pinned to one branch sees only that branch.

Sales reports

Who opens them. Anyone with the sales reports permission (report_sales:read). Cost, margin and margin percent columns appear only for people who also hold the profit reports permission (report_profit:read); everyone else sees the same report without them. The Gross margin by product report needs both permissions to open at all.

What counts as a sale. The same rule as the Business Overview: an order that was not cancelled, failed or refunded, was not refused or left as a draft at approval, and was paid, or was placed by a trade customer on credit terms. An unpaid shop checkout is an abandoned cart and is not a sale. Because every report uses this rule, no figure disagrees with the overview.

Item reports against order reports. Sales by product, category and supplier add up the lines sold, so they show item sales before tax and delivery. Sales by branch, by customer, by weekday, by hour and the Sales summary add up whole orders, so their totals equal the overview's sales exactly. Each item report prints a small table, How this adds up to the Business Overview, that takes the items listed, adds order-level discounts and rounding, tax and delivery, and arrives at the overview's sales figure.

ReportQuestion it answersRowsColumns and figuresRow click
Sales summaryHow much did we sell each day, and is it growing?One per dayOrders, sales, average order, share of the period, change against the same position in the comparison period. Headline: sales, orders, average order, tax, units. Chart: sales per day against the comparisonnone
Sales by product (item sales, top selling)Which products sell best, and which are slipping?One per product, biggest firstUnits, orders, sales, share, change, average price; with cost rights: cost, margin, margin %. Chart: top ten productsOpens the product
Sales by categoryWhich parts of the range earn the most?One per category (a product with no category is one row, "Not in a category")As above. Charts: top categories and share of salesnone
Sales by supplierWhich suppliers' goods sell the most?One per supplier (a product with no purchase on record is one row, "No supplier on record")As above. A product's supplier is the vendor of its latest approved purchase orderOpens the vendor
Sales by branchWhich branches sell the most, and which are growing?One per branchOrders, units, sales, share, change, cost and margin with cost rightsnone
Sales by customerWho are our biggest customers, and when did they last buy?One per customer, biggest first; customers who gave no name are one row, "Walk-in customer"Orders, sales, share, change, first order, last orderOpens the customer (trade customers)
Sales by weekdayWhich days of the week are busiest?Monday to SundayOrders, sales, average order, share. Headline names the busiest weekdaynone
Sales by hourWhich hours are busiest, so staff are there when customers are?00:00 to 23:00 in the business time zoneOrders, sales, average order, sharenone
Returning customersAre customers coming back, and how many are new?Returning, New, Walk-inCustomers, sales, share, change, average per customer. Headline: customers who bought, returning customers, returning share, new customers, who bought more than once, typical days between ordersnone
Sales returnsWhat comes back, why, and how much does it cost us?One per product returnedUnits, credit notes, value, share. Chart: reasons. Headline: value returned, credit notes, returns as a share of salesOpens the product
Gross margin by productWhich products earn the most, and which sell for too little?One per product, highest margin firstSales, cost, margin, margin %. Margin counts only lines whose cost was known when soldOpens the product

Business rules and edge cases.

  • Comparison. Every row shows its change against the comparison period (previous period or same period last year). A row with nothing to compare with shows a blank change, never a made-up number.
  • Customers. A customer is whoever the order names: a trade customer, a signed-in shopper, a phone number or an email. An order that names none is a walk-in and is counted apart. The same person under two phone numbers counts as two, so ask for the customer's phone at the till.
  • New against returning. New means the first sale ever falls in the period; returning means they bought before it.
  • Cost. Cost comes from the cost recorded on each line when it was sold. A line with no cost is left out of margin and the report says how much is known; it is never treated as free.
  • Long lists. A report shows its 500 biggest rows. If there were more, a notice says so and downloads are refused until the period or branch is narrowed, so a file never silently lacks rows.
  • Currencies. Reports add up the business's base currency only; orders in another currency are not converted into it.
  • Returns are credit notes by the date they were issued, not the date of the original sale.
  • No branch. A person with no branch and no company-wide right sees empty reports, never every branch.

Implementor checklist. Give the sales reports permission to sales managers and branch managers; give the profit reports permission only to people who may see cost. Confirm every product has a category and that purchase orders exist for the products each supplier supplies, or the category and supplier reports will be dominated by the "not in a category" and "no supplier on record" rows. Test: place a cash sale and a credit sale, then confirm Sales by branch equals the overview's sales and Sales by product plus tax and delivery arrives at the same figure.

Financial statements

Who opens them. People with the financial statements permission (report_financials:read). The income statement can be narrowed to one branch. The balance sheet, statement of changes in equity and cash flow statement describe the whole company, so they also need the all-branches permission, and the branch choice is not offered on them: a single branch does not have a balance sheet.

Where the figures come from. The general ledger, by the date each entry was posted, in the business's base currency. They are therefore the same figures as the trial balance for the same dates. Groups and their order follow your own chart of accounts: a heading in the chart becomes a group on the statement, so changing the chart changes the statements without any other setup. Accounts with no activity are left out. A negative amount is written in brackets.

Bank and cash accounts are not a cash flow statement. Finance → Bank and cash holds the places money sits: balances, statements, reconciliation and drawer counts. The Cash flow statement is a report that explains why the money moved in a period, and it ends on those accounts' balances and proves it.

Every statement carries a proof, drawn above it. A green line says the statement agrees with the books. A red line says it does not and shows both sides; do not rely on a statement with a red line until the difference is explained.

StatementQuestionLayoutProof
Income statement (profit and loss)Did we make a profit, and where did the money go?Revenue (sales, returns, discounts) to net sales; cost of sales; gross profit; operating expenses; operating profit; other income; net profit. Each line against the comparison period, with its change and its share of net sales. Headline: net sales, gross profit, gross margin, net profit, net marginNet profit equals what the profit and loss accounts of the trial balance add up to
Balance sheetWhat do we own, what do we owe, and what is the business worth?Assets, liabilities and equity as at the end of the period and as at the end of the comparison period, grouped as your chart groups them. Profit not yet closed into retained earnings appears inside equity, split between earlier years and the year to dateAssets equal liabilities plus equity
Statement of changes in equity (retained earnings)How did the owners' stake change, including retained earnings?Opening balance, profit for the period, capital introduced or withdrawn, owner drawings and dividends, any adjustment or year-end closing entry, closing balance, in columns: capital and other equity, retained earnings, totalOpening plus movements equals closing, and the closing equals the equity on the balance sheet
Cash flow statement (indirect method)Where did our cash come from, and where did it go?Net profit, add back depreciation, changes in working capital (receivables, stock, prepayments, creditors, taxes, customer balances); investing (equipment and other fixed assets); financing (loans, share capital, drawings); net change; opening and closing cashThe change in cash equals the movement on the cash and bank accounts

Business rules and edge cases.

  • Revenue. Revenue is the accounts the general posting setup uses for sales, sales returns and sales discounts. If none is set, every income account is treated as revenue. Any other income account shows under Other income.
  • Cost of sales is what the ledger holds. It follows the stock posting; until stock posting is live, cost of sales and gross profit are understated, and the statement says so.
  • Year-end. Profit that no year-end closing has moved into retained earnings is shown in equity, so the balance sheet always balances. When a closing entry is posted in the period it appears on the equity statement as Adjustments and year-end closing entries, and the cash flow statement shows it as its own line, so nothing is hidden.
  • Cash and bank means the accounts your payment methods post to, plus the cash and bank group of the chart.
  • Cash flow sections. Assets are sorted into investing when their name or group mentions property, plant, equipment, fixtures, vehicles, land, buildings, intangibles or investments; liabilities into financing when they mention loans, borrowings, debentures, overdrafts, leases or mortgages; equity accounts are financing. Everything else is operating. Name accounts in the chart plainly so they land where you expect.
  • Single branch. The income statement for one branch includes only entries posted to that branch.
  • Comparison. The comparison period is the period before, or the same period last year; the balance sheet compares the closing date of each.
  • Downloads carry the statement line by line with the same columns.

Implementor checklist. Give the financial statements permission only to finance staff and owners. Confirm the posting setup names sales, returns and discount accounts, that the chart's headings group accounts sensibly, that a fiscal year exists for the dates reported, and that stock posting is live before relying on gross profit. Test: post a sale, a receipt and an expense; confirm the income statement's net profit matches the trial balance, the balance sheet balances, and the cash flow statement's closing cash equals the sum of your bank and cash accounts.

Inventory reports

Who opens them. People with the inventory reports permission (report_inventory:read). Stock valuation and Slow and dead stock show what stock cost, so they also need the profit reports permission (report_profit:read). Stock is held for the whole company, so these reports have no branch choice, and all but Stock movement have no period: they describe stock as it is right now, and say so.

What counts as stock. An active product that is not deleted and is of the "inventory" kind. A service or a non-stock item is never in stock, so it is never reported as out of stock. The Business Overview's Stock health panel uses the same rule, so the counts agree.

ReportQuestion it answersRowsColumns and figures
Stock valuationWhat is our stock worth, and where is it?One per product, the most valuable firstCategory, on hand, cost each, stock value, share of value. Headline: stock value at cost, units, products stocked, products in stock with no cost recorded. Charts: value by category and by location. A small table proves the list adds up to the stock value on the Business Overview
Low and out of stockWhat must we reorder now, and how long will what is left last?Products whose available stock is at or below their reorder level; out-of-stock first, then the soonest to run outOn hand, reserved, available, reorder level, sold in the last 30 days, days of cover. Headline: out of stock, low stock, and how many of them are still selling. Chart: what is selling and running out soonest
Slow and dead stockWhat is not selling, and how much cash is tied up in it?Products with stock that has not sold in 30 daysHow long since the last sale (30 to 60, 60 to 90, over 90 days or never), on hand, cost, cash tied up, last sold date, units sold in the last 90 days. Headline: cash tied up, dead stock, share of all stock value
Stock movementWhat came in, what went out, and what was adjusted?Products with any movement in the period, the biggest change firstReceived, sold, returned by customers, returned to suppliers, adjusted and written off, net change, on hand now

Business rules and edge cases.

  • Available is on hand minus what is reserved for open orders. Low means available is at or below the product's reorder level (a reorder level of zero means only out-of-stock products are listed for that product). Out means nothing is available.
  • Days of cover is available stock divided by the average daily sales of the last 30 days. A product that has not sold in that time has no figure, because there is nothing to run out of; a product that is out of stock shows zero.
  • No cost recorded. A product with no cost has an unknown value. It is counted and named in the valuation, and it is never valued at nothing. Record a cost for every stocked product or the valuation understates the business.
  • Free gifts are not sales. A product that is only ever given away shows as not selling.
  • Transfers between locations are left out of Stock movement: they move stock, they do not change how much the company holds.
  • Long lists. Each report shows its 500 biggest rows and says when more exist.

Implementor checklist. Give the inventory reports permission to stock controllers and buyers; give the profit reports permission only to those who may see cost. Set a reorder level on every product that must not run out, record a cost on every stocked product, and mark services and non-stock items with the correct product kind. Test: receive stock, sell some, adjust some, then confirm Stock movement shows each, Low stock lists a product once it falls to its reorder level, and Stock valuation proves out against the overview.

chapters.htmlContent:
Guide 16: Van Sales & Pre-Sales (/admin/settings/sales/van-sales, and the Van sales screens under Sales)

> What is built so far. This guide describes what a company can use today: the Van sales settings screen (which of the two modes are on, and the rules every van day follows), Vans, Sales reps and Routes (set up who sells, from what, and to whom), Van days (planning a day from a route and a date) Loading (making up a load, sending it and signing for it) Running the day (the rep sends the day out and works the visits) and Selling from the van (cash and credit sales at a visit). Pre-sell orders, loading, selling, collections, the day-end count, the rep phone app, offline selling and reports are built one slice at a time; each adds its screens to this guide in the same change. The full plan is in docs/architecture/van-sales.md. Nothing here is switched on for a company until its administrator switches it on.

1. Executive Overview & Commercial Value Proposition

Operational Problems Solved

  • Stock and cash that are away from the company all day. A van leaves in the morning with stock worth hundreds of thousands of shillings and a rep who sells with no supervisor beside them. Van sales signs the stock and the float out in the morning, counts both back at night, and turns every difference into a named, approved, recorded item instead of an argument.
  • Two ways of selling, one system. Van sell is the rep who sells from the van and hands the goods over on the spot. Pre-sell is the rep who takes an order and the goods follow later. Most distributors do both; the system runs either alone or both together on the same day.
  • Unplanned loading. The load for tomorrow is worked out from the route's usual stock levels and the orders already taken for tomorrow's customers, so vans leave full of what will sell and what is owed.
  • Visits that cannot be seen. Every call on a customer is recorded with its time, its result and, when no sale was made, the reason.
  • No signal on the road. Reps keep selling and bringing orders in with no connection, and everything is taken in safely when the signal returns (a later slice; its own switch and its own permission).

Target Client Profiles

Beverage, water, bread and dairy distributors; gas and fuel dealers; FMCG wholesalers selling to kiosks and shops; agro-input and feed suppliers; any company with outside reps who visit customers on a round.

Commercial Sales Pitch & Talk Track

> "Your reps already sell outside the shop. What you cannot see today is what is on the van, what cash they hold, and which customers they actually visited. With van sales, the van is a stock location with its own till: you load it against a signed sheet, the rep sells with the customer's own prices and your discount rules, the system takes every shilling through the same till and receipts your counters use, and at the end of the day the van and the cash are counted back and any difference needs a reason and, above your limit, a second person. Orders taken on the road reserve stock the same moment, and tomorrow's load already includes them."

Measurable ROI & Safeguards

Shrinkage visible per van, per rep and per day; fewer disputed shortages; cash differences found the same evening; more calls per day; fewer stock-outs on the van; orders delivered on the customer's next round without a separate delivery cost. Every sale on a van carries a KRA-signed receipt like any counter sale.

2. Prerequisites & Configuration Sequence

  1. Branches and stock locations (Guide 13, Guide 05).
  2. Registers (tills) and payment methods that pay into a cash or bank account (Guide 11); a van's till is one of them.
  3. Customers with their price lists, credit limits and blocks (Guide 03, Guide 04).
  4. Delivery vehicles if the company uses the vehicle register (Guide 06).
  5. Van sales settings (this guide, section 4): switch on the modes the company uses.
  6. Vans, then Sales reps, then Routes, then Van days and loading (this guide, sections 4 to 6); loading also needs stock by location switched on under Inventory, and a warehouse or store to load from: a route needs a branch, and may name a van and a rep, so make those first. A route's customers must already be on the customer list, and the products of its usual stock must be kept in stock. Permissions: see section 5.

Required permission to open the settings: Van sales: settings. Held by Super Admin and Administrator by default.

3. Module & Sub-Module Architecture

Mental model. A van is a stock location with its own till. A rep sells from it. A route is the round of customers. A van day is one rep's one outing: loaded in the morning, out, back, counted, closed. A visit is one call on one customer. Pre-sold orders are taken on visits and handed over from a van day or a normal delivery run.

Upstream: products and prices, customers and credit, stock locations, registers and payment methods. Downstream: the till's shifts and Z reports, the sales ledger and receipts with KRA signing, stock movements and the books' stock value, delivery runs for pre-sold orders, and customer statements for credit sold and money collected.

Sub-modules (built as slices): Settings (built), Vans (built), Sales reps (built), Routes (built), Van days, Loading and Running the day (built) and the load planner, the rep's phone app, Day-end count and reconciliation, Offline selling for reps, Reports.

4. Interface-by-Interface Walkthrough

Settings › Sales › Van sales (/admin/settings/sales/van-sales)

A single card with these parts, top to bottom:

  1. Status line and chips. Who last changed it and when ("Never changed: both are off by default" for a new company), and two chips: Van sell on/off and Pre-sell on/off.
  2. What your reps do. Two switches, Van sell and Pre-sell, each with a plain explanation. A company may switch on one or both.
  3. Customers not on the route. Two choices: a rep may sell to a customer who is not on the route (recorded as off-route), or may sell only to the route's customers.
  4. Stock that is missing from a van. Two choices: charge the rep for what is missing, or write it off as a stock loss.
  5. A second person must decide a shortage worth more than (KES, at cost). An amount. 0 means every shortage must be decided by a second person.
  6. Stock may stay on the van overnight. A switch. Off: every van is unloaded and counted every day. On: the rest stays, signed for by the rep, and is counted when the day closes.
  7. Where the rep is when visiting. Two choices: record how far the rep was from the customer and never stop the sale, or require the rep to be near the customer to start a visit. When require is chosen, a field appears: how near counts as at the customer (metres).
  8. Reason (a list the company controls) and Save; Undo appears once something changed.

Sales › Van sales (/admin/van-sales)

The home of the module (needs Van sales: read). It shows, when van sales is switched off for the company, a card saying so with a button to switch it on in Settings (for people who hold Van sales: settings; others are told to ask an administrator); when it is on, two chips (Van sell on/off, Pre-sell on/off) and a Change these link. Below are four cards, Van days, Routes, Vans and Sales reps, each with its counts (in use, stopped; selling, paused, ended) and a button that opens its list. Vans and reps can be set up while the modes are still off.

Sales › Van sales › Vans (/admin/van-sales/vans)

A list of the company's vans, a page at a time, by name.

  1. Search box (name or stock code) and the In use / Stopped / All buttons (In use is shown first).
  2. Add a van button (needs Van sales: manage) opens the New van form.
  3. Each van shows its name, a status chip (In use or Stopped), Till open when a shift is open on its till, its branch, its stock place code (such as VAN-KDA-123X), its vehicle, the account its till cash is kept in, its cash limit, and how many products are on the van. A stopped van also shows Stopped because: and the reason typed.
  4. Buttons on a van: Change, Stop this van (for a van in use); Use again (for a stopped one).
  5. Show more loads the next page. An empty list says so and, for a new company, says to add the first van.

Sales › Van sales › Sales reps (/admin/van-sales/reps)

A list of the people who sell outside, a page at a time, by name.

  1. Search box (name, email or phone) and the Selling / Paused / Ended / All buttons.
  2. Add a sales rep button (needs Van sales: manage) opens the New sales rep form.
  3. Each rep shows their name, a status chip (Selling, Paused or Ended), what they do (Van sell, Pre-sell), email, phone, home branch, the most discount they may give, the credit they may give in a day, whether they may change a price, and, for a paused or ended rep, Paused because: or Ended because: with the reason typed.
  4. Buttons on a rep: Change (not for an ended rep), Pause (selling reps), End work as a rep (selling or paused reps), Put back to work (paused or ended reps).

Sales › Van sales › Routes (/admin/van-sales/routes)

A list of the company's routes, a page at a time, by name.

  1. Search box (name or code) and the In use / Stopped / All buttons.
  2. Add a route button (needs Van sales: manage, and at least one mode switched on) opens the New route form. When both modes are off, a notice says so and the button is not offered.
  3. Each route shows its name and code, a chip for In use or Stopped and one for what it is for (Van sell, Pre-sell, Van sell and pre-sell), its branch, how many customers it has, how many products are in its usual stock, and its usual van and rep. A stopped route also shows Stopped because:.
  4. Open route opens the route's own page.

A route's page (/admin/van-sales/routes/<route>)

Four parts, top to bottom. A route that does not exist shows the not-found page.

  1. The route. Its status and mode, its usual van and rep, and the buttons Change the route, Stop this route (asks why) or Use again.
  2. Customers on this route. The round, in order, each with its place number, name, town and phone, the days it is visited and how often, any note, and a warning chip if the customer is blocked or no longer in use. Buttons: Add a customer; on each customer Up, Down, Change days and Take off route (asks once). An empty route says so.
  3. Usual stock of the van. The products the van should start the day with, each with its quantity and unit, a product search with quantity and Add to the list, Take off on each line, and Save the usual stock (with Undo while there are unsaved changes).
  4. Who is due on a day. A date box, and the customers a rep would visit that day, in the order of the round, with a count such as Monday: 3 customers due or nobody is due.

Sales › Van sales › Van days (/admin/van-sales/days)

A list of van days, the latest date first, a page at a time.

  1. Search box (day number, route or rep) and the Open / Closed / Cancelled / All buttons (Open is shown first: a day is open until it is closed or cancelled).
  2. Plan a day button (needs Van sales: plan and at least one mode switched on) opens the Plan a day form.
  3. Each day shows its date and number (such as VDY-26-00000012), a chip for where it is (Planned, Being loaded, Out on the route, Back at the depot, Being counted, Closed, Cancelled) and one for what it is for, the route, the rep, the van, and how many of its visits are done. A cancelled day shows Cancelled because:.
  4. Open day opens the day's own page.

A van day's page (/admin/van-sales/days/<day>)

  1. The day. Its state, what it is for, the rep and van, a link Open the route, and Cancel this day (asks why) while the day has not gone out.
  2. Visits. The customers to visit, in order, each with its place number, name, town and phone, the route's note, a state chip (To visit, At the customer, Done, Skipped, Shop closed), a warning chip if the customer is blocked or no longer in use, and Added to this day by hand where it did not come from the route. While the day is planned or being loaded: Add a customer, and on each customer who has not been visited Up, Down and Take off the day.
  3. History. Everything that has happened to the day, oldest first, each with the time, who did it and, where one was given, the reason.

Loading, on a van day's page

Below the visits, for a day that has a van (a day that only takes orders has none of this):

  1. Make up the load (or Make up a top-up once the day is out). Shown to people with Van sales: plan while the day has no load that is still wanted. Load from chooses the warehouse or store (the day's own branch first). The list below is what the route's usual stock suggests: for each product the usual quantity, what is already on the van, what the warehouse has that is not promised to a customer, and how much is short when the warehouse cannot give it all. Each line has a quantity to change and Take off; Add a product adds one that is not in the usual stock. Ask for the load makes it up.
  2. Loads. Each load or top-up shows its number, where it has got to (Asked for, Approved, On its way to the van, Partly signed for, Signed for, Cancelled), where it is from, what was asked, sent and signed for on each line, and who signed and when. The buttons offered are only the next step: Approve (where the company wants a second person to), Send it, Sign for the load, Call it off.
  3. On the van now. What the van holds, from the stock records, with anything already promised.

Running the day, on a van day's page (the rep's own)

  1. Send the day out. Shown while the day is planned or being loaded. It says Ready to go or Not ready and why (for a day with a van: The van has no stock yet. Make up the load, send it and sign for it before the day goes out.). The rep counts the cash into the van's till (the float, nothing is allowed) and presses Send the day out. Anyone else sees where it stands and who sends it out.
  2. Visits, once the day is out. For each customer the rep has Arrive (the phone says where it is), then Finish: no sale (asks why), or Skip (asks why) for a customer not to be visited today, or Shop closed (asks once) if the shop is found shut. A customer can be added on the road (Add a customer) where the company allows it. Each visit shows when the rep arrived and how far from the shop, how it ended and why.

Selling at a visit, on a van day's page (the rep's own)

  1. Sell. On a visit the rep has arrived at, in a day that sells from a van. The rep adds products from what is on the van (search by name or code; only products with stock on the van are offered), types the quantity, and sees the total worked out by the system at the customer's own prices. A rep allowed to change prices sees Price for one; a rep allowed discounts sees Discount % with their limit.
  2. Paid now. The rep chooses how it is paid (cash, M-Pesa, card), types the amount handed over and, for M-Pesa or card, the reference. The screen says what is still to pay, or the change to give. Complete the sale is available only when the total is covered.
  3. On account. A rep allowed to sell on credit also has On account: the sale goes on the customer's account within their credit terms and the rep's credit allowance for the day.
  4. Sales shows what the day has sold, the total, and how it was taken (cash, mobile money, card, on account).
  5. Finish the visit. A visit with a sale is finished as sold; a visit with no sale is finished with a reason. The two cannot be mixed.

Taking an order at a visit, on a van day's page (the rep's own)

  1. Take an order. On a visit the rep has arrived at, in a day whose route takes orders (pre-sell or both) while Pre-sell is switched on. The rep searches any product (not only what is on the van, since the goods come later), types the quantity and, if the customer wants it by a day, Needed on. The system works out the total at the customer's own prices; the rep cannot type a price or a discount on an order.
  2. Take the order. Nothing is paid and nothing leaves the van. The order is an ordinary sales order: it appears under Sales Orders, its stock is held at the warehouse, and it follows the company's normal approval and credit rules.
  3. Sales on the day lists the order marked Order and shows Orders for later apart from the money taken, so the day's takings are not overstated.
  4. Finish the visit. A visit with an order is recorded as Order taken; with a sale as well, Sold and order taken. A visit with either cannot be finished as no sale.

Deliveries, on a van day's page

  1. Add an order (the planner, before the day goes out). On a day with a van on a route that sells from the van and takes orders, the planner adds an open sales order of a customer who is on the day's visits. If the order has no delivery yet, one is planned: our own riders, from the order's branch, to the customer's address (county, town and street on the customer card). An order that is waiting for approval, closed, already on a delivery, set to another delivery method, or whose stock was already issued is refused with the reason.
  2. The load counts it. The load planner adds the order's lines to what the van needs, and treats the stock the order is holding at the warehouse as available to load.
  3. Where the stock is is shown on each delivery: At the warehouse, not loaded yet, On its way to the van, On the van, or Not on the van: the load came short. A delivery can be taken off the day only while its stock is still at the warehouse.
  4. Deliver (the rep, at the customer). When the rep has arrived at the customer, each of that customer's deliveries shows Deliver, Refused and Could not deliver. Deliver asks who received the goods and carries the delivery through its steps in one go; the stock is issued from the van and the order shows delivered. Refused and Could not deliver ask why; the stock stays held on the van until it is unloaded.
  5. Finish the visit. A visit cannot be finished while it has a delivery that is not dealt with. A visit with only a delivery is recorded as Delivered.

Cash on the van, on a van day's page

  1. Cash on the van shows what the van's till should hold now (the float, plus cash sales, less cash refunds and cash taken off) against the van's limit (set on the van under Vans, Cash limit). It says Within the limit, Near the limit (from nine tenths of it) or Over the limit, and when near or over it tells the rep how much to take off. A limit warns; it never stops a sale.
  2. Take cash off the van (the rep, while the day is out or coming back). The rep types the amount, chooses where it goes (The safe, A bank run or The office) and may add a note. The amount cannot be more than the van holds. The list below shows each drop with its time and note.

Collecting money at a visit, on a van day's page

  1. Collect. On a visit the rep has arrived at, a customer who owes money has a Collect button. The form shows what the customer owes in total and the open invoices, oldest first.
  2. Take the payment. The rep chooses how the customer paid (cash, M-Pesa or card as set up for the branch), types the amount and, where the way of paying asks for one, its reference (the M-Pesa code or the card slip number). The amount cannot be more than the customer owes.
  3. What happens. The payment is recorded as an ordinary customer receipt and applied to the customer's open invoices, oldest first. Cash is also put into the van's till shift, so the cash the van should hold goes up by the same amount; M-Pesa and card go straight to the company's account and do not change the van's cash.
  4. Money collected lists each payment under the day's Sales, with the receipt number. A visit where only money was collected is recorded as Collected, and cannot be finished as no sale.

Taking goods back at a visit, on a van day's page

  1. Return. On a visit the rep has arrived at, where the customer bought goods for cash from this same van earlier (today or on an earlier day), the rep has a Return button. The form lists those sales and, for the one chosen, what can still be returned and at what price.
  2. Fill it in. The rep types how many of each product are coming back, chooses a reason from the company's list, adds a note if useful, says whether the goods are Fit to sell again or Damaged, and chooses how the customer is paid back (cash, or M-Pesa to a number). The amount to pay back is worked out from what the customer paid.
  3. What happens. A credit note corrects the customer's tax invoice, goods that are fit to sell again are counted back onto the van they were sold from (damaged goods are not counted back into stock), and a cash refund is handed over out of the van's till shift, so the van's cash goes down by the same amount. Refunds follow the company's refund approvals and limits.
  4. Goods returned lists each return under the day's Sales. A visit where goods were taken back is finished as done, never as no sale.

The rep app (/rep, on the rep's phone)

The same day, built for a thumb in sunlight. A rep signs in with their own account on the usual sign-in page and is brought back to the app; on a phone they can add it to the home screen (it is named after the company). It is never listed by search engines.

  1. My days (the home). The days that are the rep's own to run, from yesterday to a fortnight ahead, each a large tap target: the day (Today, Tomorrow or the date), the route, its state, the van, how many visits are done of the total with a bar, and Next: the customer to see. A person who is not set up as a sales rep is told to ask the office.
  2. A day (tap it). The day's state, progress and the cash on the van. Before it goes out, the Send the day out and loading panels (the rep signs for the load here). Once it is out:
  • Next stop puts the customer to see in front: who and where, Call, WhatsApp and Directions (to the customer's map pin where there is one, otherwise to the place on the card), and one large I am here button, which records the arrival.
  • Below it the same panels as the office screen, in the order a rep needs them: the visits (with Sell, Take an order, Collect, Return, Finish, Skip and Shop closed), the sales, collections and returns of the day, the deliveries, the cash and cash drops, the stock on the van, and the day's history.
  1. Same as last time. At a customer the rep has arrived at, if the customer has bought through a van before, Sell and Take an order offer Same as last time (the order number), which fills in what they last bought; the rep changes the quantities and the system prices it as always.

Coming back and unloading, on a van day's page

  1. I am back at the depot (the rep, from the day's End of the day panel). Available once every visit is finished or skipped and every delivery has its result (delivered, refused or not delivered); until then the panel says what is in the way, by name. The day moves to Back at the depot, and selling, orders, collections and returns stop.
  2. Unload the van (the rep, on a day with a van). Everything the system says is on the van goes back to the warehouse as a transfer, which leaves the van at once (or after approval, where the company asks for transfers to be approved). It appears among the day's loads as Unload, On its way to the warehouse. Stock held on the van for a delivery that was refused is let go so it can leave.
  3. Receive at the warehouse (the warehouse, with the permission to settle van days). On the unload card, the warehouse counts what came off the van. Everything that was sent is filled in; if something is missing, the count is changed and what was not counted stays on its way as a shortage to be decided when the day is settled. Stock held for a refused delivery is held again at the warehouse for its order.
  4. Start settling the day (the office). Available once the unload is received (or the van was empty, or the day takes orders only). The day moves to Being counted.

Settling and closing the day, on a van day's page

Once the office starts settling (Being counted), the Settling the day panel appears.

  1. Shortages. Each product the warehouse did not count at the unload is listed with how many are missing and what they are worth at cost. Decide (the office) asks why the stock is missing; the missing stock is then written off, and where the company's rule is to charge the rep, its value is also charged to the rep. A shortage worth more than the company's limit is decided by a manager, and says so; the rep whose van it was never decides it.
  2. The van's till. The cash in the till is counted (Cash counted in the till, with a reason if the count differs from what the till should hold) and the shift is closed through the till's own close, with its report number and difference. A difference beyond the company's allowance needs a supervisor or the approval queue, as at the counter. The rep may close their own till; anyone else must be a supervisor.
  3. Close the day (the office). Available once every shortage is decided and the till is closed; until then the panel says which is in the way. The day is Closed, and its rep, van and route are free for another day.
